issues.body:
Found by an agent-performed visual pass during the promotion gate, and verified against production. Pre-existing, so it does not block that promotion — filed on its own.

## What happens

A user creating a host picks a contact from the contact selector. The handler takes the real `ContactRow` it is handed, copies `first_name + last_name` into a free-text field, and throws the identity away.

`employers.primary_contact_id` exists as a column. `hosts/create.tsx` never sets it — zero occurrences in the file. What persists is `contact_name`, a string.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

The contact was *selected*, not typed. The system had the record in its hand and chose to keep the label instead of the link. So:

- Renaming the contact leaves every host still showing the old name.
- There is no path from a host back to the contact record a user deliberately chose.
- Two hosts sharing a contact have two unrelated strings, and nothing knows they are the same person.
- `primary_contact_id` stays empty on every row created this way, so anything downstream that relies on it sees a host with no primary contact.

This is the "enter once, use everywhere" rule, and the awkward part is that the entry already happens once — the picker is right there and working. Only the write discards it.

## Not the other findings from the same probe

The same class fired three more times and I am not filing those, because they are not the same thing:

- `externalAccountId` and `clientId` on the integrations page are identifiers in a **third-party** system — a provider's account or client reference. There is no canonical local entity for those to point at, and free text is correct.
- `name` on this same host form is the entity **being created**. It cannot reference something that does not exist yet.

The heuristic matched on the shape of the field name in all four cases. Only this one has a real foreign key sitting unused beside a picker that already resolved it.

## Fix

Set `primary_contact_id` from the selected contact's id, and keep `contact_name` only if a denormalised display copy is genuinely wanted — in which case it should be written from the linked record rather than typed, so the two cannot drift.

Decide explicitly what happens when someone types a name without using the picker. Either that is allowed and the link is simply absent, or the field should require a selection. Both are defensible; silently keeping a name with no link is what happens today.

## Acceptance

Creating a host via the contact picker stores a `primary_contact_id` that resolves to the chosen contact. Renaming that contact is reflected wherever the host's contact is shown, or the stored copy is deliberate and documented as a snapshot. A test must fail against the current handler.
issues.title: A picked contact is stored as a name and the foreign key beside it is left empty

issues.body:
Seven features tell the user they are not available yet. All seven tables exist on production. I confirmed each one under a read-only transaction:

```
signature_requests             -> signature_requests
whs_incidents                  -> whs_incidents
whs_risk_assessments           -> whs_risk_assessments
whs_policies                   -> whs_policies
people_training_day_overrides  -> people_training_day_overrides
dashboards                     -> dashboards
host_capacity_assessments      -> host_capacity_assessments
```

Every one resolves. Not one is absent.

## What the user is told

> "The safety policies database table is being provisioned. This feature will be available shortly. Contact your administrator if this persists."

The same sentence, with the noun swapped, appears on incidents, risk assessments and signature requests. Six of the seven sit on routes reachable from the navigation.

So someone opens WHS incidents, is told the system is still being set up, and contacts their administrator. The administrator finds a table that has been there all along. The message is not merely stale, it actively sends the user somewhere with a question that has no answer.

## Why this class is worth its own issue

These were written as graceful degradation, which was the right instinct when the tables genuinely did not exist. The problem is that nothing expires them. A guard that says "not yet" has no mechanism to notice that "yet" arrived, so it keeps saying it indefinitely — and it is precisely the kind of message that stops anyone investigating, because it reads as a known state rather than a fault.

That is the same shape as the case-notes banner in #2464, which said the backend was not connected while the table existed and had never matched the code. A notice explaining an absence is the most effective way to stop anyone measuring whether the absence is real.

There is an eighth instance that is worse because it cannot self-correct at all: a hardcoded refusal in the field-officer assistant tools, which will keep declining regardless of what exists.

## What "fixed" means here

Not deleting the guards. They should fire on a real failure — a table genuinely missing, or a permission denial — and say which. What is wrong is that the message asserts a cause it has not checked.

For each of the seven: confirm the feature works against the live table, remove the provisioning notice, and let a genuine error surface as an error. Where a feature turns out to be incomplete behind the guard, that is a separate finding and should be filed as one rather than left under a message that misdescribes it.

## Acceptance

Each of the seven either works, or fails with a message that names what actually went wrong. No message claims a table is being provisioned. And a check that fails when a "being provisioned" string ships alongside a table that resolves, so this cannot silently return.

## Method

Grep for the provisioning and not-connected phrasings across the app, then resolve every named table against production with `to_regclass`. Seven found, seven present. I have not audited what each feature does once its guard is removed, and that is the next question rather than something this issue answers.
issues.title: A permission error is reported to users as "this table is being provisioned"

issues.body:
Surfaced by gating #2455, where a page was written against columns that do not exist and every check in the repo passed. This issue is about why nothing caught it, because that part is estate-wide.

## The hole

`createEntityStore` takes `tableName` as a `string` and casts the result `as unknown as T`. The table name is never connected to the generated database types, so the row shape a caller declares is accepted on the caller's word alone.

The repo already knows the truth. `src/types/supabase.ts:2037` says `case_notes` has `content: string`, `subject: string`, and no `visit_type`. That file is generated from the live schema and is correct. It simply is never consulted, because the cast discards the question before it is asked.

So `tsc` exits 0 while a page writes `visit_type`, `visit_date` and `field_officer_id` to a table with none of them, and reads `content` as JSON from a `text NOT NULL` column.

## Confirmed against production

```
note_type   text  NOT NULL      subject  text NOT NULL
content     text  NOT NULL      person_id / employer_id / training_contract_id  uuid
rows: 0
```

No `visit_type`, no `visit_date`, no `field_officer_id`. `subject` is NOT NULL with no default and is collected by no page. The table has never received a row, so nothing has ever exercised the write path to find out.

## Why this is worse than one broken page

A store helper that erases the schema turns a compile-time error into a runtime failure at the moment a user presses Save. Every consumer of `createEntityStore` has the same exemption, and the failure only appears when someone finally writes a row — which, on a table with zero rows, may be a customer.

Tests do not close it either: mocking the store wholesale, which is the normal thing to do, removes the last place the mismatch could show up.

## Fix direction

Make the table name a key of the generated `Database['public']['Tables']`, and derive the row, insert and update types from it rather than accepting a caller-supplied `T`. The cast then has nothing to hide and the existing generated types start doing the work they were generated for.

That will surface existing mismatches across every consumer. That is the point, and the count of what it surfaces is the real acceptance measure for this issue.

## Acceptance

A store declared against a non-existent column fails `tsc`. A store declared against a real table with a wrong field type fails `tsc`. Then run it across the estate and report what it found, per table, rather than fixing silently.

A test asserting only that a correctly-typed store still compiles passes today and proves nothing.
issues.title: createEntityStore casts away the schema, so a page can write columns that do not exist

issues.body:
Found by the PI-run enforcer while gating #2448, by biting the guard itself rather than the code the guard protects. Not blocking — the shipped code is correct. This is about what the assertion can actually see.

## The imprecision

The unsaved-work register asserts that every registration gated on an `open`-style flag is backed by a reset. The `resetBesideOpen` clause looks for a bare `reset\(` within 400 characters of `set<Flag>(true)`.

It does not check *whose* reset it found.

`integrations.tsx` is the first file with several forms to carry gated registrations, and it exposes this immediately. Removing **every** `apiForm.reset()` from the open paths still passes 128 of 128, because the span that satisfies the clause is `documentServiceForm.reset({…})` in `handleEditIntegration` — a different form's reset, sitting close enough in the file to count.

The enforcer printed the satisfying span rather than inferring it, so this is measured rather than reasoned.

## Why it matters

The clause exists to catch exactly the defect this PR closed: a registration gated on a flag whose panel does not reset, so a cancelled draft stays declared and unreachable. A proximity match that any nearby reset satisfies will report that as backed while it is not, and it will do so most reliably in the multi-form files where the mistake is easiest to make.

## Fix

Bind the pattern to the form the registration names: `${form}\.reset\(` rather than `reset\(`. One token.

## Acceptance

Removing a given form's resets from its open paths fails the assertion for that registration and no other. A nearby unrelated form's reset does not satisfy it. Both directions asserted, so the fix cannot be achieved by making the clause never match.

## Related, already recorded

The same assertion documents a companion false negative in its own comment: `reset(getValues())` re-baselines while keeping every value, so a dialog using it satisfies the guard and still hands back a cancelled draft. Same character — the clause tests for the presence of a call rather than for what the call does. Worth fixing together and worth one sentence in the header saying what the clause does and does not establish.
issues.title: The unsaved-work register accepts a different form's reset as proof

issues.body:
Found by looking at the deployed page, after the operator pointed out schema vocabulary on a sibling screen (#2459). This one is worse, and it is worth stating why before the list: the page's own opening sentence is written exactly right, and everything beneath it contradicts that sentence.

The intro reads:

> Add a field here and it becomes a real field on that kind of record everywhere it appears — Incidents, Contacts, Training Plans and VET Qualifications read your changes immediately.

That is the product, in the user's nouns, promising something valuable. Below it is a database diagram.

## What is actually on screen

**SQL types and constraints as labels.** Every row carries `TEXT`, `DATETIME`, `TEXTAREA`, `BOOLEAN`, `NUMBER` or `MULTISELECT`, and `NOT NULL` in red. A person deciding whether a field should be required is not helped by `NOT NULL`, and the red suggests an error rather than a rule.

**Raw column names, including plumbing that must never be touched.** On the Contact card alone: `tenant_id NOT NULL`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `custom_fields`, `company_resolution_status`. On Client: `primary_contact_name_snapshot`, `primary_contact_email_snapshot`, `primary_contact_snapshot_updated_at`, `anzsic_code`, `asri_id`, `stars_org_id`, `parent_employer_id`, `is_worksite`.

These sit at identical visual weight to `phone`, `email` and `first_name`. Someone invited to "add a field to that kind of record" is shown thirty rows, most of which are our bookkeeping, with nothing marking which ones are theirs. That is worse than jargon — it is an invitation to break something.

**Table names as card subtitles**: `contact`, `lead`, `client`, `apprentice`, in lowercase monospace under the friendly card title. The friendly name is already there. The table name adds nothing a user can act on.

**"45 entities"** as the count under the search box.

**An unexplained `SYS` badge** on every card.

**"React Flow" printed in the bottom-right corner** — the diagramming library's own branding, rendered in the product. That is a third party's watermark on a page a customer sees.

## Why this matters more than wording

The screen presents itself as a place to shape records, and what it actually shows is our storage. A user cannot tell which fields are theirs to change, which exist for the system, and which are denormalised copies that will be overwritten. There is no safe first move.

The fix is not a copy pass. It is deciding what belongs on this screen at all: the fields a tenant can meaningfully add or rename, separated clearly from system columns, with types named the way the person choosing them would say it — text, date, yes/no, list — and required shown as a property rather than a constraint keyword.

## Sibling screens, same class

- **#2459** — form layout builder: `Entity: people`, `Context: default`, a `people / default` badge, and an empty state claiming "All fields placed" when there are none.
- **Form Layouts index** — subtitle reads "Drag-and-drop form layouts for entity create/edit views". `entity create/edit views` is our vocabulary, and the same `people / default` badge appears on the row.

## Acceptance

A tenant administrator who has never seen this page can identify which fields they may change, add one, and predict where it will appear, without knowing what a column, an entity, or a null is. No SQL keyword, no table name, and no third-party watermark on the page.

Evidence: screenshots captured on `d.crm.crm7.app` while signed in, at the development head.
issues.title: The schema builder shows users a database, not their records

issues.body:
Raised by the operator from a screenshot of `/settings/form-layout-detail`. Three separate D8 failures visible on one screen, none of which any gate this session would have caught, because every gate was checking structure and none was reading the words.

## 1. The empty state says the opposite of the truth

The Fields panel shows a count of **0** and the text **"All fields placed"**, beside a canvas reading **"No sections yet"**.

The condition is `unplacedFields.length === 0` at [FormLayoutBuilder.tsx:253](crm7/src/components/ui-customization/FormLayoutBuilder.tsx#L253), which is vacuously true when there are no fields at all. So a brand-new layout tells the user everything is done at the exact moment nothing exists. It is not merely unhelpful, it actively points away from the next action.

An empty layout should say there are no fields yet and offer the way to get one. That is the same gap as #2450, seen from the other side: there is no way to create a field here, and the screen also declines to mention that any are missing.

## 2. Schema vocabulary is rendered directly to the user

Four places on this one screen: the `people / default` badge beside the title, `Entity: people`, `Context: default`, and `Layout — People`.

`entity_type` and `context` are column names. "people" is a table. D8.3 asks for labels in the user's nouns; a person managing a form does not have an entity or a context, they have *what this form is for* and *where it is used*.

The page already knows how to do this — it looks up `entities.find(e => e.name === entity_type)?.label` and only falls back to the raw value. The label lookup is there and the field name beside it is not.

## 3. A ticket reference became a user-visible object name

The layout is called **"AD-7 exercise"**. AD-7 is an internal reference to the `tenant_entity_records` write path in `EntityTableWidget`. It is a fixture row in `form_layouts` owned by the E2E tenant `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000e2e`.

It is confined to that tenant, so no customer sees it, and it is still worth fixing twice over: fixtures that survive in a tenant people demo and screenshot from will be read as product, and nothing prevented a developer's ticket ID from becoming an object name in the first place.

## Also on this screen

**Deploy Scope: All / Org / Locked.** Three words that do not say what they do. What is deployed, to whom, and what does Locked prevent? A first-time user cannot predict the outcome of pressing any of them, which is the D8.3 test.

**"Save from the builder to create a new version of this layout."** This explains a mechanism rather than offering an action, on a panel that has a Save button eight centimetres away.

## Acceptance

Someone who has never seen this screen can say what the layout is for, what state it is in, and what to do next, from the screen alone. Specifically: the empty state names the absence and offers the remedy; no column or table name appears in any visible label; and every deploy control says what it will do.

Not a copy pass over the same nouns. If a word cannot be replaced with something a user would say, that is a sign the control needs rethinking rather than renaming.
issues.title: Form layout builder shows schema nouns, a false empty state, and a ticket ID as a name

issues.body:
Surfaced while correcting a comment in #2448, and it is worth its own ticket because the unsaved-work registry cannot help here.

## What a user loses

Start editing the on-costs section, or employee numbering, under settings configuration. Switch to another tab before saving. Switch back. The field is empty and the edit is gone. Nothing warned, and nothing can be recovered.

## Why the usual protection does not apply

Both cards sit inside a `TabsContent`, and there is no `forceMount` anywhere in the file, so radix unmounts them when the tab changes. The component holding the draft is the thing being destroyed.

That is why this cannot be closed by declaring the work to the unsaved-work registry. A registration protects a draft that still exists — it arms a prompt before a reload or an organisation switch. Here the draft is already gone by the time anything could ask, and the action that destroyed it is an ordinary in-page tab click that no guard intercepts.

## Not the same as the four page-level forms

Four other forms on this page are declared at page level, so their form objects outlive the tab. For those, switching away and back really does show the edit, and treating them as retained work is correct. Only these two are positioned inside the tab content in a way that unmounts them.

That distinction is the whole point of filing this separately. A uniform fix across the page would be wrong in one direction or the other, which is exactly how the original mistaken comment arose.

## Fix direction

Either `forceMount` on the two tab panels so they keep their state across a tab change, or lift their state above the tab boundary the way the other four already are. Lifting is the more consistent answer, because it makes all six forms on the page behave the same way and removes the special case rather than papering over it.

This is a change to the page's shape, not to the unsaved-work class.

## Acceptance

Type into on-costs, switch tabs, switch back, and the text is still there. Same for employee numbering. Then confirm the unsaved-work prompt still fires on a reload with that edit pending, so the fix does not achieve retention by dropping the registration.

A test must fail against the current markup. Asserting the field is empty after a tab switch passes today and encodes the defect.
issues.title: Switching tabs mid-edit silently discards on-costs and employee-numbering drafts

issues.body:
Umbrella for the class that #2449 turned out to be one member of. Established by the enforcer gating #2452, which swept three axes rather than one and found twelve defective sites where my own token sweep had found a single one.

## The class, stated as a symptom

**A numeric input that treats a valid zero as absent.** That sentence is the class, and it has two halves that share no vocabulary, which is why searching for a spelling misses most of it.

**The payload half.** `onChange(e.target.valueAsNumber || null)`. A typed `0` is falsy, so it is stored as null. This is #2449 and it is fixed by #2452.

**The display half.** `value={x || ''}`. A *stored* zero renders as a blank field. Same symptom for the user, and it contains no `valueAsNumber` at all.

A third shape belongs to the class and matches neither search, because its fallback is not zero: `parseFloat(raw) || 1` on a penalty multiplier silently substitutes a different number rather than clearing the field. That one is money and is filed separately as R80.4 #313.

## Count

Twelve defective across the axes swept: the token, the idiom with a mismatched fallback, and the display side across all 137 `type="number"` inputs in 70 files in six apps. #2452 fixes one of the twelve.

Five were re-opened and confirmed by hand, including a leave balance on a person's record with `min={0}`, and both the hours and the rate on an invoice line. Those are pages users reach every day.

## The pattern to copy, which already exists here three times

The correct discriminator is the raw string, not falsiness, because HTML value-sanitization forces the value to an empty string for anything unparseable — so "no parseable value" and "NaN" are the same set, and zero is neither.

`SchemaDrivenFilterForm.tsx:213`, `DynamicFieldRenderer.tsx:131` and `award-rates/create.tsx:758` each do it correctly already: check the raw string, and use `??` rather than `||` on the display side. React Hook Form's own `getFieldValueAs` discriminates the same way, which is why the two compliance pages registering with `valueAsNumber: true` are not affected.

## Priority note

Fix the reachable ones first. `fetchCustomPage` filters on `is_published`, and production holds two custom pages, neither published and neither containing a field, so the surface #2452 repairs is one no user currently reaches. The eleven remaining sit on pages they do.

## Acceptance

Per site: typing `0` stores `0` and displays `0`; blank and unparseable input still yield the intended absent value; and where the fallback is a non-zero number, that substitution is either removed or made visible. Tests must fail against the current expression at each site — a test using only positive values passes everywhere today.
issues.title: Numeric inputs that treat a valid zero as absent: 12 sites, two halves, one fixed

issues.body:
Found by the PI-run enforcer while gating #2448. Pre-existing and byte-identical before that PR, so it is not caused by it.

## What a user loses

Open settings configuration. Start editing the Email section. Before finishing, save the General section. The Email draft is silently destroyed, and it is marked clean on the way out, so nothing warns and nothing offers it back.

## Cause

Saving any one section invalidates the `['tenant-settings']` query. The hydration effect then re-runs and resets **all four** page-level forms, not just the one that was saved. The other three are re-baselined to the freshly fetched values, so any unsaved typing in them is both discarded and reported as clean.

## Why it matters beyond the immediate loss

The unsaved-work register treats these settings sections as retained work: the reasoning is that a settings tab keeps its edits when the tab changes or a panel collapses, so the draft is still there and still losable, and therefore must be declared. That reasoning is correct about tab changes. This defect holes the same premise from a different direction, because there is one ordinary action on the page that does not retain the work at all.

The registration is still right. A user who types into Email and reloads should be asked. But a user who types into Email and saves General should not lose it, and today they do.

## Fix direction

Reset only the form whose section was saved, or re-baseline the others without clobbering dirty fields. The general shape is that a refetch triggered by one section should not be allowed to overwrite in-progress edits in another.

## Acceptance

Type into one section, save a different one, and the first section keeps both its text and its dirty state. Then reload and confirm the unsaved-work prompt still fires for it, so the fix does not achieve retention by quietly dropping the registration.

Tests must fail against the current effect. A test that saves the only dirty section passes today.
issues.title: Saving one settings section silently destroys unsaved edits in the other three

issues.body:
Found incidentally while fixing #2447. Not caused by that work, and deliberately left alone there so the fix stayed one change.

## The collision

Two components register a droppable under the same id in [FormLayoutBuilder.tsx](crm7/src/components/ui-customization/FormLayoutBuilder.tsx):

- `SortableSection` via `useSortable({ id: \`section-${section.id}\` })`
- `SectionDropZone` via `useDroppable({ id: \`section-${sectionId}\` })`

dnd-kit keeps droppables in a map keyed by id. Two registrations under one key means exactly one survives, and which one survives is a React effect-ordering detail rather than anything the code states.

## Why it has not bitten yet

It has not caused a visible bug because, after #2447, both registrations carry an identical data payload, so the drag handler behaves the same whichever one wins. That was a deliberate choice in that fix: make the handler indifferent rather than gamble on the ordering.

That is a mitigation, not a resolution. It holds only as long as the two payloads stay identical, and nothing enforces that. The next person who adds a field to one payload, or changes a mount order, or wraps one of the two in a conditional, gets a behaviour change with no obvious cause and no failing test.

## What to do

Give the two registrations distinct ids, so the drop zone and the sortable section are separately addressable, and let the handler tell them apart by their payload `type` as it already does elsewhere. Then the map has one entry per registration and the effect ordering stops mattering.

## Acceptance

A test that both registrations are simultaneously present and independently resolvable, so reintroducing a shared key fails. Asserting only that drag still works would pass today, with the collision intact, which is exactly why this is worth its own guard rather than relying on the existing drag tests.
issues.title: Two components register the same dnd-kit droppable id, so one silently wins

issues.body:
Reported by the copilot-customization-audit lane, which modelled the service in a VM against a mocked response contract. I verified it against the source and the live schema, and there are two consequences their report does not name.

## The defect

In [customPageService.ts:139](crm7/src/services/customPageService.ts#L139), `savePageRevision` writes the revision row and checks it, then writes the page itself and checks nothing:

The revision insert destructures its error and throws on it. The `custom_pages` update discards both the error and the affected-row count, and the function returns the revision as though both writes landed. A row-level security refusal, or an update that matches no row, is indistinguishable from success.

## Consequence one: the user watches their work disappear while being told it saved

The caller re-reads the page after saving, which was written as a safety measure and is commented as one. When the page update silently failed, that re-read returns the *old* layout, and the handler assigns it straight into the editor. The user's arrangement is replaced on screen by the version they were trying to overwrite, and the success toast fires in the same breath, quoting a version number that never incremented.

So the safety measure is what destroys the visible work. Without the re-read the user would keep their layout in the canvas and merely fail to persist it.

## Consequence two: the revision history silently corrupts

`custom_page_revisions` in the production baseline has a primary key on `id` and a foreign key on `page_id`. **There is no unique constraint on `(page_id, version)`.**

The version is computed as the page's current version plus one. When the page update fails, the page's version does not move, so the next save computes the same number again and inserts a second revision at that version. Nothing refuses it. `getPageRevisions` orders by version descending, so the duplicates tie and their relative order is arbitrary. A user reading the history sees two rows both labelled the same version, with no way to tell which is which.

The restore path calls the same function, so restoring a revision carries the identical failure.

## What this is not

This is executable service behaviour, not proof that live row-level security currently refuses this update. Nobody has shown a real tenant hitting it. The defect is that the code cannot tell the difference, so if it ever happens the user is told the opposite of the truth.

## Acceptance

- A rejected update and a zero-row update must both fail loudly. Neither may return a revision or fire a success toast.
- The page row and the revision must agree after a save, or the save must not report success.
- Two saves racing must not produce two revisions at one version. Decide whether the fix is a unique constraint on `(page_id, version)`, an atomic function that writes both, or a version taken from the database rather than computed in the client, and say why.
- On the deploy: edit, save, reload, and confirm what is on screen is what is stored. Then the restore path the same way.

Tests must fail against the current service. A test that only exercises the success path passes today.
issues.title: A custom page save reports success when only the revision was written

issues.body:
Reported by the copilot-customization-audit lane. I verified the absence.

## What a user cannot do

Open a form layout or a custom page for editing, and you can arrange fields that already exist. You cannot create one. There is no inline path from "this section needs a field that does not exist yet" to having it, so the work stops and the user goes looking elsewhere for wherever fields are defined.

## Verified

`FieldCreateDialog` exists at `packages/schema-builder/src/components/FieldCreateDialog.tsx` and is wired only into `SchemaCanvas`. Zero occurrences in all three of the relevant files: the builder itself, and both hosts, [form-layout-detail.tsx](crm7/src/pages/settings/form-layout-detail.tsx) and [custom-page-edit.tsx](crm7/src/pages/settings/custom-page-edit.tsx).

## What "done" means here

This is the round-trip test, and it is the whole point of the ticket. Finishing the task must not require leaving the page. The dialog opens over the builder, the new field is created, and it appears in the section the user was working in, already placed and selected.

The unsaved layout must survive it. A user who has spent five minutes arranging sections and then creates a field must not come back to an empty canvas, and must not be asked to save first as the price of creating a field. If the create genuinely cannot happen without a save, that is a design answer that needs stating, not an accident to discover after losing the arrangement.

## Acceptance

Open either host, add a field that does not yet exist, and have it land in the intended section without navigation. Then reload and confirm both the field and the surrounding layout persisted. Both hosts, because they are two mount sites and a fix to one is not a fix to the other.

## Sequencing

This queues behind #2447. That fix is in `FormLayoutBuilder.tsx` and this work touches the same file plus both hosts, and two lanes in one file is a collision this estate has already paid for once today.
issues.title: No way to create a field from inside either form builder

issues.body:
Measured by the PI-run enforcer on crm7#2433: a test probe ran **120 seconds to a hard kill** despite `testTimeout: 30000` in the vitest config. A hang inside a render loop does not yield to the per-test timeout, so the value that is supposed to bound a stuck test does not bound this one.

This has now bitten three times in one day on the same repository, each time from the same family — a mock whose object identity changes per render against a component that depends on a stable callback, producing an infinite render loop that presents as a slow test rather than a failing one. Two of the three were abandoned and their files deleted, correctly, because a hanging test in the tree is worse than the gap it was meant to close: in CI it reads as a timeout rather than a regression.

What is missing is the outer bound. `testTimeout` governs an individual test's own promise; it does not stop a synchronous render loop. The job needs a **job-level timeout** (`timeout-minutes` on the step or job in `ci.yml`) so a hang fails fast and loudly with a message that names the file, instead of consuming the runner until the platform kills it.

Worth pairing with a note in the testing guidance: when mocking a dependency that a component passes to `useEffect` deps, hoist the mock to a module-level singleton. The failure mode of getting that wrong is not a wrong assertion, it is a hang.
issues.title: A hanging test is not bounded by testTimeout: a render loop ran 120s to a hard kill; the job needs its own timeout

issues.body:
Found by running the visual probe **inside the page-grid editor** on `/settings`, which the ordinary probe never enters. Both are **pre-existing**: the identical probe against production (`crm.crm7.app`, `2dfd75a`) produces the same two failures, so they are not introduced by any pending promotion.

**1. In edit mode, dark-mode cards lose their accent glow.** The probe measures max shadow chroma `0.0166` against a required `0.05` — every layer is at or below the ambient ink's own chroma. This is the V-C7 class the estate has fixed twice before. Note the contrast with the same page **outside** the editor, where the glow is present and measurably chromatic (`lab(74.67 -44.21 -10.26 / .28)` and `oklch(0.769 0.132 191.7 / .3)`). So the tokens are right and something in the editor's card rendering drops them — a canvas-card wrapper or an override that applies only while editing.

**2. A free-text input where a canonical entity exists** (`freeTextEntity`), in both themes. The gate's rule is that a field naming a canonical entity must be an FK-backed selector, and this is the one-shot-non-conformance class the DRY doctrine exists to stop.

Also recorded, not a defect: `canvasColumns` stays UNKNOWN even with the column control open and reading 2, because the probe cannot confirm a column count from a uniform grid — "geometry is CONSISTENT with 2 columns but cannot confirm it, a uniform grid is ambiguous by construction". Closing that needs the columns *interaction* (set a preset, observe the layout change), not a static read. Worth saying plainly because it means the class is not closable by probing alone, and a future run should not report it as passed.

Why this matters beyond the two findings: **the editor is a state the visual gate has never measured.** Outside it, `/settings` reads 0 FAIL across both themes and four widths; inside it, the same page is a BLOCK. Any surface with a mode the probe does not enter has an unmeasured half.
issues.title: The page editor is an unmeasured state: dark cards lose their glow in edit mode, and a free-text field names a canonical entity

issues.body:
Found by a read-only authz review (`bsuite-rls-authz-red-team` + `auth-supabase`) over the tenant-scoping diffs; report at `~/.claude/projects/-home-braden-Desktop-Dev-bsuite/evidence/2026-09-05/authz-review-tenant-scoping-2431-2432-2436.md`, finding F2. Not an authorisation bypass — the server re-evaluates `acting_scope_tenant_id()` on every request regardless — but the banner's own docblock claims something it does not do.

`ActingAsBanner`'s `['acting-as-scope']` query has no `refetchInterval`, the QueryClient default is `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, and the component mounts once per tab inside the persistent `MainLayout`. The 30-second tick only recomputes the expiry label from the row already held. So a scope change made in another tab, or on another device, is not noticed until an unrelated reload — while the docblock says such changes are always noticed.

This is the FOLLOW-83 mismatch class recurring on a narrower path: what the page shows and what the server applies drift apart, and the component that exists to close that gap is the one carrying the stale claim.

Two shapes, either acceptable: a short `refetchInterval` on that query, or a cross-tab nudge over `storage` / `BroadcastChannel` — the app already does the latter for `logoutSync`, so the pattern exists. Whichever is chosen, the docblock's claim should be made true or narrowed to what the code does.
issues.title: ActingAsBanner cannot see a scope change made in another tab, while its docblock says it always can

issues.body:
Raised by the PI-run enforcer while gating crm7#2436, as a residual outside that PR's scope.

`resolveTenantSelection` honours a **localStorage** tenant at its third step when the server pin (`profiles.current_tenant_id`) is NULL. For a person with two or more memberships and no server pin, that step picks the organisation the browser last remembered and proceeds. That is a guess: NULL from the server means "they have not chosen", and the fail-closed rule is that a NULL meaning unknown is never read as a choice. The browser's memory is not the person's decision — it can be a different person on a shared machine, or a membership since revoked, or simply stale.

The consistent behaviour is the one `useTenantConfirmation` already implements for the confirm path: when there is no server pin and more than one membership, **ask**, and write the pin through `set_current_tenant` on the answer. localStorage can remain a hint for which option to preselect; it must not be the selection.

Pre-existing, not introduced by #2436; recorded here so the class has an owner. Related: the resolution order in `acting_scope_tenant_id()` (acting-as row → profile pin → sole membership → NULL) and `bsuite_correction` records on deterministic guesses.
issues.title: resolveTenantSelection: a localStorage tenant is honoured when the server pin is NULL — that is a guess for a multi-tenant user, and it should ask

issues.body:
Measured on the promotion candidate (d.crm.crm7.app at `fbd887c`), signed in, in the page editor on `/settings` at a 1440px viewport.

The column-count control is reachable and accepts input: the four-click editor path lands on `input[aria-label="Column count"]`, and setting 12, 6, 4 and 2 each reads back correctly. The rendered layout does not respond. Holding every reading until two samples 1.5s apart agreed, all four presets produce **one identical layout**, with card width pinned at 531px in every case.

The container is the reason and it is worth stating precisely: at a 1440px viewport the `/settings` content container measures **1080px**, and the control only rescales the `lg` breakpoint, which needs 1200px. So this is the documented "inert below a 1200px container" condition, now confirmed by interaction rather than inferred. The same control does act elsewhere — presets give distinct layouts on `/dashboard` at a wider container.

Two earlier passes disagreed with each other here because I read the layout before it settled; a short settle produced "4 columns gives fewer columns than 2", which is an artifact and not a real observation. Only the agreement-held readings above should be quoted.

The user-facing consequence is that on any page whose container is under 1200px, a control that visibly accepts a value silently does nothing. Either it should rescale the active breakpoint rather than only `lg`, or it should say it does not apply at this width. Pre-existing and outside the current promotion's scope.
issues.title: Column-count control is inert wherever the container is under 1200px (/settings is 1080px)

issues.body:
Measured on the promotion candidate (d.crm.crm7.app at `fbd887c`), signed in as `braden@braden.com.au`.

`/notifications` is built, returns 200, and renders real data — "Total 2, Unread 2", two genuine forwarded emails with title, message, priority and date. It is also unreachable and inert, in two independent ways.

**No entry point exists anywhere in the application shell.** Enumerating every anchor in the shell for `notif` in either the text or the href returns zero. The header carries Toggle Sidebar, CRM7, Edit page, Switch to dark theme, the org name and User menu — no bell. The user menu opens with no notifications entry. The only way a person reaches this page is by typing the URL.

**The rows do not link to anything.** Inside `main`, the anchor count is zero. The only controls are "Mark All Read" and a priority filter. So a notification about a specific thing cannot be opened to reach that thing — the deep link does not exist, rather than being broken.

`/settings/notifications` returns HTTP 200 while rendering "404 - Page Not Found", so anything that guesses that path fails silently rather than redirecting.

This is the dead-route class, and the standing rule is that a dead route is unbuilt work: find the spec and build it out, never delete it. Two pieces are owed — an entry point with an unread count, and a per-notification destination. Neither is in the current promotion's scope, which is why this is filed rather than blocking it.
issues.title: Notifications are unreachable: no entry point in the shell, and no deep link on the rows

issues.body:
`switchTenant`'s own-membership branch does two writes that must succeed or fail together:

1. `platform_admin_stop_acting()` — clears any live acting-as row.
2. `set_current_tenant(p_tenant_id)` — pins the selection in `profiles.current_tenant_id`.

Between them the caller is in a state neither of them intended: the scope has moved and the
selection has not. crm7#2425 handles that with a compensating path — `scopeChanged: true`, and
the caller reloads into whatever scope now applies — which is correct and is not the same thing
as the two writes being atomic.

**Why the interim was chosen.** The atomic version is a new `SECURITY DEFINER` function on
`platform_admin_acting_as`, and that did not belong in a branch already carrying the crm7#2398
promotion. The compensating path is the smaller change and closes the observed defect.

**What atomic would look like.** One RPC that stops acting and sets the current tenant in a
single transaction, so a failure leaves neither applied. It also removes the reload-on-partial
behaviour, since there would be no partial state to reload into.

**Why this ticket exists rather than a comment.** The interim is only correct while somebody
remembers it is an interim. Filed so it does not become permanent by silence.

Raised from the crm7#2398 promotion review. See crm7#2425 for the compensating fix and its tests.
issues.title: Make stop-acting and pin-selection atomic in switchTenant

issues.body:
## The gate checks less than its name suggests

`scripts/check-control-boundary-contrast.mjs` reads a control tag's own
**literal source text** — it finds `<input>`/`<select>`/`<textarea>`/
`<button>` (and a curated list of component wrappers), extracts that tag's
opening-tag text, and pattern-matches the class string written directly
inside it. It does not evaluate JSX, does not resolve `className`
expressions, and cannot see into a helper function's return value.

**This means the gate does not check controls. It checks controls whose
classes are written inline.** Any control whose `className` is computed —
via a `cn(someHelper(props), '...')` call, a `useMemo`, a variant map, or
any other indirection that isn't a literal string sitting in the tag's own
text — is invisible to it, regardless of what that computed string actually
contains.

Found via crm7#2423: `TrainingYearCalendar.tsx`'s `dayCellClasses()` returns
a bare `border-border` for its `'non-scheduled'` branch, consumed as
`className={cn(dayCellClasses(cell), '...')}` on a real `<button>`. The gate
scans that tag's literal text — `cn(dayCellClasses(cell), 'cursor-pointer
hover:border-border')` — sees no `border-border` substring in it (the actual
offending string lives inside `dayCellClasses`'s function body, dozens of
lines away), and reports nothing. The banked ratchet count (5) has held
through every fix landed against this gate today because none of those
fixes changed *what the gate can see* — only *how it classifies what it
already sees* (which variants are transient, whether a bracket value's
"active" names a pseudo-class, whether a downgrade on hover counts). This is
a different, deeper gap: a real violation that will never be counted no
matter how correct the variant logic becomes, because the scanner never
reads the line it lives on.

## Why this matters beyond the one file

Any page or component in either `crm7` or the shared `@bsuite/*` packages
that computes its control's className via a helper — a status-to-style
map, a `cva()` variant function, a `useMemo`-derived class string — sits in
this same blind spot. The true violation count is `>= 5` (the banked
ratchet), not `= 5`; the gap between them is currently unmeasured.

## What would close it

The gate would need to at minimum recognise the common `cn(helperCall(...),
'...')` / `cn(someVariable, '...')` shape and either (a) flag it as
`unknown` rather than silently passing when the tag's className expression
contains anything other than string literals, so the gap becomes visible
in the report rather than invisible to it, or (b) statically resolve simple
local helper functions (a small, closed set of cases — a `switch`/`if`
returning literal strings — rather than attempting general JSX/TS
evaluation). Option (a) is far cheaper and is the honest minimum: a check
that cannot prove a computed class is safe should say so, not stay silent.

## Related

crm7#2423 — the one confirmed live instance this blind spot let through.
issues.title: control-boundary-contrast gate only reads inline className literals — computed classes are invisible to it

issues.body:
## What

Every non-scheduled day cell in the training year calendar renders a control
boundary at 1.06:1 (light) / 2.36:1 (dark) against the page — the bare
`border-border` divider token — instead of the 3:1 minimum WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11
requires for a control's identifying boundary. This fires on every
non-scheduled cell whenever the calendar is rendered `interactive`.

## Where

`src/components/training/TrainingYearCalendar.tsx`:

- **Line 126** — `dayCellClasses(cell)`, the helper that computes each day
  cell's class string.
- **Line 141** — the `'non-scheduled'` branch:
  ```ts
  case 'non-scheduled':
    return cn(base, 'border-border bg-muted/40 text-muted-foreground')
  ```
  `base` (line 129) sets `border border-transparent`, so this branch is the
  only one that swaps in a real border color — and it swaps in the bare
  divider token, not `border-border-interactive`.
- **Line 255** — where it's consumed, on a real `<button>`:
  ```tsx
  <button
    key={cell.date}
    type="button"
    className={cn(dayCellClasses(cell), 'cursor-pointer hover:border-border')}
    aria-label={dayAriaLabel(cell)}
    aria-pressed={cell.entry?.status === 'training'}
    onClick={() => onToggleDay?.(cell.date, nextToggleKind(cell))}
  >
    {cell.dayOfMonth}
  </button>
  ```

## Fix

Change line 141 to use `border-border-interactive` (or another
already-registered ≥3:1 token) in place of the bare `border-border`, matching
the pattern every other branch in the same `switch` already follows (they all
route through `bg-*`/text tokens without introducing the low-contrast
divider as a control boundary). Re-run `node scripts/check-control-boundary-contrast.mjs`
after the fix — it will not currently catch a regression here (see
crm7#2424, the companion gate-blindness issue), so this needs to be verified
by eye or a targeted test until that gap is closed.

## How this was found

Found while investigating crm7#2422 (a different fix to the same gate) —
not itself part of that PR's scope, filed separately per the enforcer's
review.
issues.title: TrainingYearCalendar non-scheduled day cells fail control-boundary contrast (1.06:1, WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11)

issues.body:
## Blocked by

`@bsuite/workflow-canvas` is **not published to npm** (`npm view @bsuite/workflow-canvas` → 404, checked 2026-09-01). crm7 resolves every `@bsuite/*` dependency from the registry, so adding it would break `pnpm install` and CI.

## The debt this forced

The graph contract that `packages/workflow-canvas/src/schemas.ts` OWNS is currently re-declared in two other places:

| Copy | Why it could not import the package |
| --- | --- |
| `crm7/src/lib/workflows/workflowGraph.ts` | package unpublished; also a React package with an `@xyflow/react` peer, and the first caller is `api/ai/chat.ts` on Vercel Edge — a chat endpoint must not bundle a canvas renderer to describe a process |
| `business-suite-unified/supabase/functions/feature-builder-ai/workflow-graph.ts` | an edge function cannot import from `src/`, let alone `packages/` |

Three copies of one contract will drift. When they do, the symptom is not a build error — it is a workflow that saves and then cannot be reopened, which reads to the user as a document that vanished.

## What holds it together in the meantime

- `crm7/src/lib/workflows/workflowGraph.contract.test.ts`
- `business-suite-unified/src/lib/feature-builder/__tests__/edge-fn-contract.test.ts`

Both assert the field-level bounds and the loose-object envelope against the package's source, and both **skip loudly** (never silently green) when `packages/workflow-canvas` is absent from the checkout.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `@bsuite/workflow-canvas` is published, and crm7 depends on it at a pinned version.
2. `crm7/src/lib/workflows/workflowGraph.ts` keeps only the outline→graph builder and the layout constants; its schema half is deleted and imported from the package instead.
3. `crm7/src/lib/workflows/workflowGraph.contract.test.ts` is deleted — it exists only to guard the duplication.
4. The edge-function copy stays (an edge function genuinely cannot import from `packages/`), and `edge-fn-contract.test.ts` stays with it.
5. `pnpm typecheck` and the workflow test suites pass in crm7 after the swap.

## Validation loop

§9.1 output-equivalence. **Equivalence target:** `buildWorkflowGraph` must produce a byte-identical graph for the fixture outline in `workflowGraph.test.ts` before and after the swap, and `serialiseGraph` must accept and reject exactly the documents listed in the contract test's `accepted`/`rejected` tables.

## Cross red-team

claude-code verifies the evidence rows before flip-to-done.

## Skills to load

`bsuite-pnpm-monorepo`, `check-dead-duplicate-code`, `test-verify-before-completion`

## Self-report on divergence

Yes — mandatory. If the published package's bounds differ from either copy, say so and reconcile rather than loosening a schema to make the test pass.

## Context

Introduced by Phase 4: crm7#2300 and business-suite-unified#1087.
issues.title: Publish @bsuite/workflow-canvas and delete the crm7 contract duplication

## Measured, not estimated

**71 routes, 292 card slots, on production**, signed in, one page reused serially to avoid the concurrent-navigation contamination that voided two earlier datasets.

| | |
|---|---:|
| slots measured | **292** |
| `itemChrome` on | 292 of 292 |
| slots painting **2+ card surfaces** (box in a box) | **171 (58%)** |
| slots painting exactly 1 | 121 |
| slots painting 0 | 0 |
| routes with at least one doubled slot | **62 of 71** |
| routes clean | 7 |
| routes with no card slots at all | 2 |

## This is not the doubled-bottom-border defect

`@bsuite/page-builder` 2.3.1 fixes `Math.ceil` row over-allocation — a grid item a few px taller than its card, so the item's edge shows below the card's. That is **one doubled edge**. What is measured here is **two complete painted card surfaces nested in one slot** — an outer frame at one radius around an inner card at another. Row arithmetic cannot remove a second painted surface. The two should be confirmed separately rather than closed together.

## How it happened — both changes were correct

1. `@bsuite/page-builder` ≤ 1.0.7 painted grid chrome unconditionally.
2. **2.0.0 turned it off by default**, and the reason is recorded in [analytics/index.tsx](src/pages/analytics/index.tsx): *"~90% of the estate nests its own `<Card>` inside the slot and was drawing a box inside a box."*
3. crm7 then set `itemChrome` page-wide — [pageGridLayoutAdapter.tsx:101](src/components/platform/pageGridLayoutAdapter.tsx#L101), `restProps.itemChrome ?? true` — to restore the ~45 slots 2.0.0 had left bare.

Each step was right. **Their composition re-created the exact defect step 2 existed to remove.**

## What the data rules out

The obvious fix would be to flip the adapter default back to `false`. **The measurement says that is not safe.**

I expected the split to fall along the two authoring patterns, which would have made this a one-line change. It does not: **all 271 resolvable slots are `DraggableCardPage`, and 161 double while 110 do not.** The split is per-page, not per-pattern. Flipping the default would correctly un-frame 161 slots and **strip 110 slots that have no card of their own**.

6 of 69 routes could not be resolved to a source file and are excluded from that 271 rather than folded in silently.

## The direction is already ruled

From the same file: *"Giving the widget its own `<Card>` is durable, is what the other ~988 crm7 slots already do, and carries the 12px card radius ruling for free."*

So the endgame is: **adapter default `false`, and ~110 slots gain their own `<Card>`.** That is a programme, not a patch — which is why this is an issue with the full route list rather than a PR.

issues.body:
## Context

Follow-up from crm7#2061 (note.110, "Back to X nav links styled inconsistently"). PR (this repo, branch `fix/issue-2061-back-to-x-consistency`) fixed the one genuinely bare/unstyled instance and introduced a shared `BackButton` component (`src/components/common/BackButton/`), but a full re-derivation of the sibling count turned up a much larger and differently-shaped class than either the issue or the prior PR (#2100) estimated. This issue tracks the remainder honestly rather than letting it look silently closed.

## What re-deriving the count actually found

Not "some plain text, some buttons" as hypothesized. Measured by reading each call site's surrounding JSX (not just grepping the string), virtually every back-navigation affordance in this codebase is **already** a real `<Button>` (or routed through `EmptyState`'s button-rendering `action`/`primaryAction` prop). The real defect is **wording and styling drift across four independent phrasings of the same control**, plus one genuinely bare link:

| Wording variant | Search | Real matches | Already a real `<Button>`? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `"Back to X"` | `grep -rn "Back to "` | 106 (1 prose false-positive excluded) | 105/106 — 1 bare `<Link>` (fixed this PR: `src/pages/portal/host-reports.tsx`) |
| `aria-label="Go back"` (icon-only) | `grep -rn '"Go back"'` | 75 raw, 73 real (2 are onboarding-wizard prev-step controls, a different affordance) | 73/73 — but 1 used `variant="outline"` instead of the other 72's `ghost` (fixed this PR: `vet/qualifications/[id]/structure.tsx`); icon size also split 58×`h-4 w-4` vs 14×`h-5 w-5` (not fixed) |
| `"Return to X"` | `grep -rn '"Return to '` | 9 | 9/9 |
| bare `"Back"` (no "to X") | `grep -rn '>Back<'` (sampled) | ~30 | not individually re-verified per-site; sampled entries are `<Button>`-wrapped |
| literal `"← Back"` (arrow character, not an icon component) | `grep -rn '"← Back"'` | 3 | 3/3 — all `<Button>`, but using a text glyph instead of the `ArrowLeft` icon used everywhere else |

**Icon choice also varies for the identical action**: `ArrowLeft` (majority), `ChevronLeft` (at least `src/pages/hosts/[id].tsx` and others — verify `ChevronLeft` isn't also legitimately used for calendar prev/period controls before treating a hit as this class), and the literal `←` character above.

**Running total measured: ~218-220 real back-navigation call sites across at least 4 wordings and 2 icons.** This is almost certainly not the full population — the bare-`"Back"` sample was not individually verified, and there may be more wordings/icons not yet searched for. State a fresh denominator before touching this; do not assume the count above is final.

## What this PR fixed (see the PR for evidence)

- The 1 confirmed bare/unstyled instance (`portal/host-reports.tsx`).
- The 1 confirmed variant-outlier in the "Go back" icon-only class (`vet/qualifications/[id]/structure.tsx`).
- Consolidated 6 byte-identical "Back to WHS" duplicates onto the new shared `BackButton` component.
- Introduced `src/components/common/BackButton/` as the canonical shared affordance (supports both the labeled and `iconOnly` shapes).

## What's left (this issue)

1. **Unify wording.** Pick one of "Back to X" / "Go back" / "Return to X" / bare "Back" as the standard (recommend "Back to X" for the labeled case — most discoverable per crm7#2061's own framing — and reserve icon-only for tight header rows) and migrate the remainder onto `BackButton`.
2. **Unify icon.** Standardize on `ArrowLeft` (already the majority); replace `ChevronLeft` and literal `←` usages.
3. **Unify icon size** in the icon-only class (16px vs 20px split, 58 vs 14).
4. Re-verify the bare-`"Back"` sample (~30 sites) individually — it was sampled, not exhaustively confirmed, in the sweep that produced this issue.
5. Consider a lint rule (`bsuite/no-hand-rolled-back-button` or similar) that flags a `<Button>` wrapping an `ArrowLeft`/`ChevronLeft` + navigate/Link combination outside of `BackButton` itself, so the class can't silently regrow.

## Separate, more important finding: the round trip is lossy regardless of styling

Live-verified against production (`crm.crm7.app`, signed in as `e2e@crm7.app`): list pages (`/leads` confirmed; `/hosts`, `/mentors` read the same way in source) keep filter/search/sort/pagination state in plain component `useState`, not the URL and not a persisted store. Typing a filter on `/leads`, opening a lead, and clicking its "Go back" button returns to a bare `/leads` with the filter silently cleared — confirmed live (`filterSurvived: false`). This is independent of whether the back control is styled as a button or a plain link; it happens because the list component unmounts and remounts with default state. Fixing it needs the list pages to read/write filter state via the URL (or a persisted store) and rehydrate on mount — a larger, cross-cutting change out of scope for a "make the back buttons consistent" PR, but worth its own ticket since it costs users real work (re-entering filters) every time they use the very affordance this issue is about.

## Skills to load

`bsuite-fix-the-class-not-the-page`, `bsuite-page-grid-layout` (for any list-page filter-state work), `test-playwright`.
issues.title: Back-navigation affordances: 4 wording variants + icon/variant drift across ~220 call sites

issues.body:
## What #2060 / #2105 found and fixed for ONE page

`placements/[id]/edit.tsx` destructures `{ selectedItem, error, errorCode, update }` from `usePlacementStore()` (a `createEntityStore` instance). Two fields, one mechanism:

- The record-load guard: `if (error || !placement) { return <Placement not found /> }`
- A failed `update()` call sets that SAME store's `error`/`errorCode` fields (`createEntityStore.ts`'s `update()` action: `set({ error: message, errorCode: extractErrorCode(err), ... })`)

So a **rejected save** (wrong data, a CHECK constraint, RLS, anything) sets `error`, and on the very next render the page replaces the entire edit form with "Placement not found" — even though the record loaded fine and is sitting right there in `selectedItem`. #2060 quoted this exact symptom: *"her placements come back as 'not found'"* after a save the constraint rejected, not a missing record.

PR #2105 fixed this for placements specifically: the save-failure branch now reads `error`/`errorCode` to build an actionable toast, then explicitly clears them (`usePlacementStore.setState({ error: null, errorCode: null })`) before the next render, so the "not found" guard can't fire off stale write-path state.

## The same shape exists elsewhere

`createEntityStore` backs **93 stores** (`src/stores/*Store.ts`). A grep for the guard shape (`if (error || !X)`) across `src/pages` found 35 matches; cross-referencing against `{ selectedItem, error, update }` destructuring + an `await update(...)` call in the same component confirms at least these six ALSO have the identical mechanism (unverified beyond this pair-check — a proper fix needs to read each one, not just grep):

- `src/pages/contracts/training/[id]/edit.tsx` (`useTrainingContractStore`)
- `src/pages/mentors/[id]/edit.tsx`
- `src/pages/communications/template-edit.tsx` (`useCommunicationTemplateStore`)
- `src/pages/vet/training-packages/[id]/edit.tsx`
- `src/pages/hosts/[id]/edit.tsx` (`useHostEmployerStore`)
- `src/pages/progress-reviews/reviews/[id]/edit.tsx` (`usePerformanceReviewStore`)

**One wrinkle that rules out a single blanket fix at the store level**: at least three OTHER consumers (`src/pages/field-officers/actions/index.tsx`, `src/pages/communications/template-create.tsx`, `src/pages/communications/template-edit.tsx`) already read the store's `error` field directly as their OWN save-failure toast description (`description: error || 'Failed to update template.'`). So `error` is currently doing double duty across the estate — some consumers correctly use it as "did the record fail to LOAD", others already (ab)use it as "did the last WRITE fail" for their own messaging. Retargeting `error`/`errorCode` to load-only in `createEntityStore.ts` would fix the guard-tripping bug for everyone in one place, but would silently degrade the save-error specificity for those consumers unless each one is migrated to a new field (e.g. `mutationError`/`mutationErrorCode`) at the same time.

## Why this wasn't done as part of #2105

#2105 is scoped to crm7#2060 (the placements charge-rate constraint). A central fix in `createEntityStore.ts` touches all 93 stores and needs every consumer that reads `error` for a write-path message audited and migrated in the same change — that's a proper standalone piece of work with its own review, not a rider on a single-page bug fix. Filing this so it doesn't get lost.

## Suggested fix shape

Add `mutationError` / `mutationErrorCode` to `EntityState<T>`, set them (not `error`/`errorCode`) from `create`/`update`/`remove`/`bulkUpdate`/`bulkDelete` on failure, leave `error`/`errorCode` set only by `fetch`/`fetchById`. Migrate the ~3 known consumers that read `error` for a save message today, then the six edit pages above (and whatever the exhaustive audit turns up) get the "not found" fix for free with zero page-level changes.
issues.title: 6+ other *Store edit pages share the stale-error-blanks-the-form bug fixed for placements in #2060

issues.body:
Measured on `d.crm.crm7.app` as `e2e@crm7.app` (address echoed into evidence per the skill), 8 cells per route — light and dark × 1440/1024/768/390. **Every value below was re-confirmed against production**, so all of these are pre-existing and none were introduced by the promotion being gated. Filed separately per ruling V-2.

Companion to #2084, which covers `/dashboard`.

---

## `/sales/pipeline-flow` — BLOCK

**1. The minimap paints pure white on dark — L = 1.0000 exactly.**
`.react-flow__minimap` renders `rgb(255,255,255)`, 200×150, in **both themes**. On the dark canvas that is a **19.25:1 white slab**. This is exactly the V-C1 class the probe exists to catch: a screenshot reads it as "a light minimap", and only compositing to OKLCH shows it hitting the pure endpoint.

**2. Two-thirds of the pipeline is off-canvas below 1024px.**
At 768 and 390, **only 2 of 6 stages sit inside the canvas rect**. `fitView` clamps at React Flow's default `minZoom` 0.5, so nodes render at 90×34 and the rest simply fall outside. The page promises a "visual deal-stage graph"; on a phone it shows a third of one. Raising `minZoom` (or fitting with padding on a smaller floor) is the fix.

**3. Zoom controls are effectively invisible in dark — 1.19:1.**
Zoom In / Zoom Out / Fit View icons measure **1.19:1** against their own button. The icon inherits `lab(93.001)` from crm7's dark text token onto a light control surface. WCAG 1.4.11 needs 3:1 for controls.

*Note:* V-C6/C7/C8 are structurally **N/A** here — this is a full-bleed React Flow route with 0 cards and no `.react-grid-layout` root, so those classes have zero subjects. Recorded as not-applicable rather than passed.

---

## `/settings/users` — BLOCK

**4. The columns control is INERT.** UNKNOWN closed as **FAIL**, not passed. The documented 3-click path was run: the dialog opens, `page-editor-edit` clicks cleanly — and then nothing. **Before/after DOM identical.** A control that updates state but never the layout is cosmetic, and cosmetic is a FAIL.

**5. "Remove" button fails contrast in dark — 3.84:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement**, `lab(48.9 73.0 48.2)` on `rgb(15,20,29)` at 12px, twice per cell. Identical on production.

**6. The Subscription Plans tab has zero controls of its own.** It states billing "remains centralized in Business Suite" and **links nowhere**. Its sibling tabs all carry working controls. A dead end with a signpost and no road.

---

## `/settings/schema-builder` — BLOCK

**7. Dark-mode elevation is a no-op on all 45 entity cards.** `box-shadow` resolves to ambient ink only — `oklch(0.080 0.0200)`, chroma **0.0166**, below the 0.05 glow floor. The cards read flat against the canvas in dark.

**8. At 390 the canvas is 390×582 with 26% of it permanently covered** — the dismissible quick-start toast takes 16% and the fixed bottom nav another 10%.

---

## `/people` — REVIEW

**9. Three distinct card shadows across 11 cards** in light mode — 6 flat, 4 with `lab(44.8 21.0 -75.5/0.1) 0 1px 3px`, 1 a second flat variant. Dark is clean. Same surface, three elevations.

**10. `color-scheme` is `normal` in dark** on the root and all three real scroll containers, so **UA scrollbars paint light on a dark page**.

---

## Worth recording

While measuring `/settings/users` the probe observed the app banner **"AWAITING SCHEMA · NOT A FAULT"** with the database at `20260920000000` — i.e. the app correctly tells the user its schema is behind rather than rendering broken. That is good behaviour and worth keeping.
issues.title: Visual gate: a pure-white minimap on dark, two-thirds of the pipeline off-canvas on mobile, and a columns control that does nothing

issues.body:
Found by the ruling V-1 visual gate while inspecting `/dashboard` for a promotion. **All eleven are pre-existing and every one was re-confirmed against production** (`crm.crm7.app/dashboard`, same account) — none were introduced by the change being gated. Filing rather than bundling, per ruling V-2.

Measured across 8 cells: light and dark × 1440 / 1024 / 768 / 390.

## The ones that cost a user something

**1. Two complete navigation systems render simultaneously (768–1023px).**
A persistent 255×1024 sidebar *and* a fixed mobile tab bar (`fixed bottom-0 ... z-45 lg:hidden`). `lg:hidden` hides the bar only at ≥1024, but the sidebar begins at 768 — so the whole iPad-portrait band gets both. Confirmed absent at 390 and 1024.

**2. That fixed bar occludes content, and the footer reserves no space for it.**
- At 768: bottom 56px of the footer hidden — copyright cut mid-sentence at "Relationship Management." Sidebar entries clipped: "R8 Calculator" half-cut, **"Conduit ATS" fully hidden**.
- At 390: the footer link **"A Braden Group Company" is entirely behind the bar and unreachable.**

**3. The "Open Jodie" FAB overlaps a footer link at every desktop width — and will intercept its clicks.**
`div.fixed bottom-4 right-4 z-50`, 56×62. At 1440 it covers 40px of the 167px-wide "A Braden Group Company" link, rendering it "A Braden Group Con". At `z-50` over a link, the click lands on the FAB. Same at 1024 and 768.

**4. "Pipeline Overview" is inert.**
The only one of seven grid cards with **zero interactive descendants** — 0 links, 0 buttons. It shows Pipeline Value, Deals Won, Active Accounts, Leads Generated and offers no route to the pipeline, on a page whose nav has a "Sales Pipeline" entry. Its six siblings carry 1–3 links each; the KPI strip above it is properly wired. Acting on any number in that card means leaving the page by hand.

## Layout failures in the 768 band

**5. Footer wordmark overprints the copyright** — right edge 354 vs left edge 346, an **8px negative gap**, legible as "CRM[7]Customer". Glued at 1024 (+2px), fine at 1440 (270px).

**6. All four KPI labels ellipsised at 768** — the label box is pinned to 94px while the icon takes the rest: "Active Opportunities" is 140px into 94px, cut 33% to "Active Oppo…". Clean at 1440/1024/390.

## Density

**7. At 390 the scrollable well is 212px of an 844px viewport** — 2822px of dashboard read through a 212px slot. Cause is a permanently pinned 273px footer *outside* the scroller plus the 56px tab bar. On production without the preview banner it is 410px — still under half the screen, so **the pinned footer is the structural cause, not the preview banner.**

**8. 392px of empty canvas below the last card at 1440** — 25% of scrollable content blank. Not grid slack: `.react-grid-layout` ends 6px after the last card; the empty run belongs to the canvas wrapper beneath it. 317px at 1024.

## What was NOT evaluated

**V-C6 (canvas columns) is UNKNOWN, not passing.** The columns control is not in the resting DOM, and interaction was forbidden because the inspection ran as a real user account — `user_preferences` is keyed by user and shared across environments, so a drag would have permanently rewritten that operator's real saved layout. Being re-run as the seeded CI identity, where interaction is safe.

## What passed

V-C1 (pure endpoints), V-C3, V-C4, V-C5, V-C7, V-C8, V-C9 clean on all 8 cells. Theme signals agreed everywhere — `class` and `data-theme` matched on every cell, no divergence. Body ground `lab(95.476)` light / `lab(3.998)` dark, neither a pure endpoint.

V-C10 passed **on presence of accessible names only** — that does not establish anything is keyboard-reachable, and should not be read as if it did.
issues.title: Dashboard: eleven measured layout defects, all live in production — two nav systems at once, a FAB that eats a link, and an inert card

issues.body:
Two findings, one long-standing directive: **anything reachable via raw JSON should also be reachable through a non-coding UI path.**

## What's wrong

- **Long-standing directive, repeated again this pass.** Operator, repeat_offence=true: "Advanced json ok, but anything available via json should be done through non-coding means. This is always and has been a long standing directive." (note.120, at `/admin/data`)
- **Concrete instance of the same gap**: developers need to actually interact with the data here — import/export CSV/XLSX, and downloadable/re-uploadable import templates. Operator: "Must be able to import and export csv and xlxs and create import templates to download and use to re-upload." (note.124, same route)

## Done means

- Every capability currently reachable only via raw JSON on `/admin/data` (and by extension, any similar surface) has a non-coding UI equivalent — an advanced JSON mode may remain available alongside it for developers, but is never the only path.
- CSV/XLSX import and export work from the UI, including a downloadable import template that can be filled in and re-uploaded without hand-editing JSON.
issues.title: JSON-only / API-only workflows have no non-coding UI path for import, export, or data interaction

issues.body:
Five smaller display defects across crm7, grouped because they're all "a record shows the wrong or missing representation of itself or its relationships" — not one root cause in code, but one class of UX debt worth fixing together.

## What's wrong

- **Raw database ID shown as the record's ID** instead of a proper Employee ID / Training Contract ID / USI once those exist. Operator: "Why is database ID displaying in full as their ID? Once Placed an Employee ID created. Training Contract ID should also be available as a primary identifier once set. Same with USI." (note.072, at `/charge-rates/import-r8`)
- **Entity field picker can't select all entities** — picking "person" exposes `person_id` from Supabase but not the person's name, and there's no way to add the person's name as an available field. Operator: "selecting person shows the person_id from supabase but not the persons name and there is no way to select the persons name in the available fields when 'add field'" (note.086, at `/settings/data` and `/admin/data`)
- **"Back to placement" and other detail-page nav links** should be buttons everywhere, not styled inconsistently per instance. Operator: "This is specific example but this should be a button for all." (note.110)
- **Person record doesn't list associated placements/engagements.** Operator: "Person record should have a list of all placements and engagements we have records for." (note.113)
- **Known member `caris@mbawa.com` is missing from the member list** at `/admin/data`, and appears to only have a `.json` representation. (note.119)

## Done means

- Records display a human-meaningful identifier (name, Employee ID, Training Contract ID, USI) instead of a raw UUID, wherever one exists.
- The entity field picker exposes the display-name field for every entity, not just its foreign-key ID.
- Detail-page "back to X" links are consistently styled as buttons.
- The person record surfaces all associated placements and engagements.
- caris@mbawa.com appears correctly in the member list, and the underlying cause of the `.json`-only representation is understood and fixed, not just this one row patched.
issues.title: Record-display papercuts: raw database IDs shown instead of names/labels, unstyled nav links, missing member, and no placements/engagements list on the person record

issues.body:
Three findings, one theme: crm7's edit and navigation model routes users away from where they are instead of letting them work in place.

## What a user cannot do

- **Edit the dashboard in place.** Editing sends the user to a separate page-builder screen that only creates a brand-new page — the ability to add elements directly to the live page in edit mode existed recently and is now missing again. Operator, repeat_offence=true: "We did recently have the ability to add new elements on page but this is now missing again." (note.010) — this reads as a **regression**, not a missing feature.
- **Edit any dashboard-reachable option without a forced new-page detour.** Operator: "Every option here should be editable on the page i'm on unless a completely new page is wanted and intended." (note.011)
- **Keep orientation while working.** General complaint, high severity: "Generally, I'm having to go in an out of pages and re-orient myself. The whole ux is terrible." (note.049)

## Done means

- Editing the live dashboard adds/edits elements in place by default; a genuinely new page is only created when explicitly requested.
- An audit of dashboard-reachable options identifies which ones currently force a new-page flow unnecessarily, with each one either fixed or explicitly justified.
- Since note.010 is flagged as a regression of previously-working behaviour, check version history for when in-place editing was lost — per D-63 in bsuite#1967 ("regressions outrank new work").
issues.title: Dashboard editing forces a new-page flow instead of in-place editing, and overall in-app navigation loses orientation

issues.body:
Two findings on the same data path: crm7's award-rates surface doesn't display or import correctly, and the intended source (R8) is not actually wired up as the source.

## What a user cannot do

- At `crm.crm7.app/payroll/award-rates`: **no wages are visible**, the period column just says "percent" instead of a real label, and there's no description shown for the row. Operator: "No wages are visible" (note.007).
- At `d.crm.crm7.app/charge-rates/import-r8`: the **import UX forces the user to hand-code** the input, and **R8 itself doesn't export in the format the importer expects** — it should be possible to pull straight from R8 instead of hand-authoring JSON. Operator: "This is horrible UX, its forcing the USER to code again, and r8 doesnt export like this. It should be able to pull in from R8." (note.069)

## Why these are one issue

Both are symptoms of the same missing link: crm7's award-rate display and import paths are not actually reading from R8's computed rate data (see also bsuite#1684, the architectural ruling that Charge Calculations are R8-owned by doctrine but authored in crm7 — this is a second, independent instance of the same drift, on award rates rather than charge rates).

## Done means

- The award-rates page shows real wage figures with a correctly labelled period column and a visible description per row.
- Importing a rate from R8 requires no hand-coded JSON — either a direct pull-from-R8 action, or an export format from R8 that this importer consumes without transformation.
issues.title: Award rates page shows no wages, mislabeled columns, and forces hand-coded JSON import instead of pulling from R8

The `fairwork-enhanced` edge function name suggests Fair Work award-rate logic, not email composition — its presence as a blocking dependency on the compose page load may itself be a mis-wired call (e.g. a shared layout component pulling in an unrelated data fetch). Worth checking whether this call is actually needed on this page before fixing it as a 503.

## Feature-index scope

crm7 module rows for `Communications inbox` and `Compose page` — check `sibling_class`/`sibling_count` to see whether other messaging-adjacent surfaces share the same broken read/compose path.

- An email in the inbox opens and its content renders.
- The compose page loads without a failed request, and if `fairwork-enhanced` is genuinely required there, it returns 200 with real data; if it isn't required, the call is removed.
