issues.body:
## The observation

`crm7#1768` (*"the E2E credentials were set and no workflow read them"*) merged at **2026-08-17T04:23:57Z**. It is correct and it fixed a real, serious hole — a green gate over 111 skipped tests.

**Its immediate second-order effect has not been noticed, and it is now blocking every lane.**

Measured at **05:19:09Z**:

| Started | Branch | State |
|---|---|---|
| 04:43:52 | `fix/ad8-xero-sync-health` | in_progress |
| 04:44:59 | `fix/d80-module-visibility-hidden-modules` | in_progress |
| 04:45:48 | `lane/v2-v4-v5-v11-controls` | in_progress |
| 04:51:36 | `lane/v2-v4-v5-v11-controls` | in_progress |
| 04:52:46 | `fix/pf3-pf4b-provable-redundancies` | in_progress |
| 04:54:52 | `fix/pf3-pf4b-provable-redundancies` | in_progress |
| 04:57:29 | `chore/bsuite-ui-1.1.0` | in_progress |
| 04:57:52 | `fix/e2e-a11y-forms` | in_progress |
| 04:58:38 | `fix/po1-field-officer-landing-queries` | in_progress |

**Nine concurrent full-browser runs. Zero completed.** The oldest has been going 35 minutes. The only `completed` run in the window failed at `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` on a dependency-bump branch — i.e. it never reached the tests.

## Why this is a change, not a coincidence

Before the fix, the suite finished in **24.8 seconds**:

```
[auth.setup] CRM7_E2E_EMAIL / CRM7_E2E_PASSWORD not set. Writing empty
             storage state — authenticated tests will skip themselves.
111 skipped
 15 passed (24.8s)
```

It was fast because it was not testing anything. Now it runs all **126** specs, in a real browser, and nine lanes are doing that simultaneously on a shared runner pool.

## Why it matters

A gate nobody can get through is failed differently from a gate that passes wrongly, but both stop work. `e2e` is the last pending check on multiple open PRs right now, so the practical effect is that **no PR in this repository can go green**. If it stays this way the predictable response is that someone marks `e2e` non-required, which quietly restores the exact posture `crm7#1768` just fixed.

**Nothing here argues for reverting `crm7#1768`.** The fix is right. What is missing is the capacity and sharding work that a suite which actually runs was always going to need, and which nobody had to think about while it was skipping.

## Reproduction

```bash
date -u +%H:%M:%SZ
gh run list -R GaryOcean428/crm7 --workflow="E2E Tests" --limit 10 \
  --json status,conclusion,createdAt,headBranch \
  --jq '.[]|"\(.status)\t\(.conclusion//"-")\t\(.createdAt[11:19])\t\(.headBranch)"'

# the "before" number, on any run created before 2026-08-17T04:23Z:
gh run view 31956277180 -R GaryOcean428/crm7 --log | grep -E "skipped|passed"
# → 111 skipped / 15 passed (24.8s)
```

## Suggested next steps, in order of cheapness

1. **Measure one full green run end to end.** Nobody currently knows how long the real suite takes, because it has never completed in CI. Everything below is guesswork until that number exists.
2. **Add `concurrency:` with `cancel-in-progress` on the E2E workflow**, keyed by PR. Two of the nine runs above are *superseded runs on the same branch* — `lane/v2-v4-v5-v11-controls` and `fix/pf3-pf4b-provable-redundancies` each hold two. That is free capacity.
3. **Shard** with Playwright's `--shard` across a matrix, once (1) gives a duration to divide.
4. **Consider a smoke subset as the required check** and the full suite on a schedule or on `main` — but only with an explicit assertion of how many specs the smoke subset executed, or this reintroduces the D-92 defect in a new costume.

## Do not fix this by making the gate optional

The whole point of `crm7#1768` and of the new *"Report how many specs actually executed"* step is that a suite must state what it ran. Marking `e2e` non-required, or reintroducing a skip-on-missing-credential path, restores a gate that cannot tell "checked nothing" from "found nothing" — bsuite#1966, operator directive D-92.

**Filing is not fixing.** Nothing in this issue changes the runner situation.
issues.title: [P1][ci] Nine concurrent E2E runs, none finishing — the V-1 fix turned a 25-second no-op gate into a saturating one

issues.body:
## The ruling

Operator directive 2026-08-13, **D-83**:

> **Proceed with the nine NULL-status rows** — eight FutureBuild plus one Braden Group — dry run first, output for review before commit. **Do not touch the twelve `unresolved` rows in bsuite Platform**: `unresolved` means resolution ran and failed, and that is a real signal in my own demo tenant. **Do not drop the constraint.** The rule is correct; only its application was wrong.

## What is live now — measured 2026-08-17

```sql
select coalesce(award_rate_resolution_status,'<NULL>') as status,
       t.name as tenant, count(*)
from placements p left join tenants t on t.id = p.tenant_id
group by 1,2 order by 1,2;
```

| status | tenant | rows | with charge_rate |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `<NULL>` | Braden Group | 7 | 0 |
| `<NULL>` | bsuite Platform | 1 | 0 |
| `<NULL>` | Demo Organisation — CRM7 | 5 | 0 |
| `manual` | Braden Group | 1 | 1 |
| **`manual`** | **bsuite Platform** | **12** | **12** |
| `manual` | FutureBuild Academy | 8 | 8 |

**Zero rows carry `unresolved` anywhere in the database.**

All twelve bsuite Platform rows share one timestamp — `2026-08-06 07:03:46.244379+00` — so they were rewritten in a single transaction, and all twelve have `award_rate_id IS NULL`.

## Two halves of the ruling: one satisfied, one already spent

| Clause | State |
|---|---|
| Proceed with the nine NULL-status rows (8 FutureBuild + 1 Braden Group) | **Done.** All nine are `manual` with a charge rate. |
| Do not touch the twelve `unresolved` bsuite Platform rows | **Already changed — before the ruling existed.** |
| Do not drop the constraint | **Honoured.** `placements_resolved_rate_required_chk` is live and now `convalidated = true`, i.e. it genuinely enforces rather than merely blocking edits. |

## Why this is not a lane disobeying an instruction

Migration `crm7/supabase/migrations/20260806165000_unfreeze_placement_rate_provenance.sql` applied on **6 August**, seven days before the 13 August directive was written. Its `UPDATE` predicate is:

```sql
where charge_rate is not null
  and (award_rate_resolution_status is null
       or award_rate_resolution_status = 'unresolved')
```

It swept `unresolved` and `NULL` together, because at the time both were simply "rows frozen by a NOT VALID CHECK that Postgres re-checks on every update". The distinction the operator later drew — that `unresolved` *means resolution ran and failed*, and `NULL` means it never ran — had not been stated when the migration was authored.

**No dollar figure was changed.** `manual` asserts provenance only: a human set this rate rather than it being resolved from an award. Every one of the twelve has `award_rate_id IS NULL`, so none was ever award-resolved.

## What was actually lost

The ability to tell, in the operator's own demo tenant, which placements had a **failed resolution attempt** versus which were simply typed in. That is a diagnostic signal about the resolver, not about the money.

## The decision — three options

**Option A — accept the loss, record it, move on.** *Recommended.*
Restoring `unresolved` re-creates the exact P0 the migration cured: the constraint is now `VALIDATE`d, so writing `unresolved` back onto a row that has a `charge_rate` would be **rejected outright** by Postgres. To restore the label the charge rates would have to be nulled first, which loses real data to recover a diagnostic. The twelve rows are in `bsuite Platform`, a demo tenant with no client exposure. Cost: one line in the directive's status record.

**Option B — restore the signal without re-freezing.** Add a nullable `award_rate_resolution_last_error` (or a row in the existing charge-rate audit log) recording that these twelve had a failed resolution before 2026-08-06, then re-run the resolver against them and let it write a truthful current result. Cost: one small migration plus a resolver run. Keeps the constraint intact. Choose this if the *resolver failure* is the thing worth knowing, rather than the label.

**Option C — restore `unresolved` literally.** Requires nulling `charge_rate` on twelve rows or dropping the constraint. **Not recommended** — the ruling itself says do not drop the constraint, and nulling the rates destroys more than it recovers.

## Not a defect, checked and disproved

The migration header warned: *"The code fix accompanies this migration; without it, an edit that clears award_rate_id would re-freeze the row."* A grep for `award_rate_resolution_status` in `src/pages/placements/[id]/edit.tsx` returns **zero**, which reads like the code half never landed. It did — the rule lives in the shared helper `withRateProvenance(...)`, called at `edit.tsx:340`, with the reasoning in a comment above it. **The zero was an artefact of grepping for a literal that a helper hides.** No action needed on the write path.

## Reproduction

```sql
-- 1. no unresolved rows survive
select count(*) from placements where award_rate_resolution_status = 'unresolved';   -- 0

-- 2. the twelve, one transaction
select id, charge_rate, award_rate_id, updated_at
from placements p join tenants t on t.id = p.tenant_id
where t.name = 'bsuite Platform' and p.award_rate_resolution_status = 'manual'
order by updated_at;      -- 12 rows, all 2026-08-06 07:03:46.244379+00

-- 3. the constraint is real now, not merely blocking
select conname, convalidated, pg_get_constraintdef(oid)
from pg_constraint where conname = 'placements_resolved_rate_required_chk';
```

**Filing is not fixing.** This issue changes nothing; it puts a decision in front of the operator that would otherwise be lost in a directive nobody re-reads.

issues.body:
`avetmiss-export` cannot succeed against production's schema. It fails at the **"Fetch source data"** step on every call, before the ZIP is built — so the function has never produced an export.

Found while building an end-to-end rehearsal proof for a *different* defect in the same function (crm7#1678, the undeclared `claims`). That fix is correct and merged, but **the line it repaired is unreachable on the real schema**, so it changes nothing operationally until this is resolved.

## Measured against production `tuybltdrdefjblnplpqo`, read-only

| reference in the function | present in production |
|---|---|
| `apprentices.dob` | **no** |
| `apprentices.postcode` | **no** |
| `apprentices.address_line1` | **no** |
| `qualifications.anzsco_code` | **no** |
| table `subject_enrolments` | **no** — has never existed in any migration |
| storage bucket `avetmiss-exports` | **no** |
| *control:* table `apprentices` itself | yes |

The control matters: the query discriminates, so these zeros are the schema's answer and not a broken probe. The function also references `apprentices.sex`, `state_code`, `country_code` and `suburb`, none of which exist either.

## Why nobody noticed

**BSuite is not RTO software** — AVETMISS data is *captured*, not *reported on* (operator, 2026-08-13). Nothing in the product calls this function in anger, so a total failure produced no signal. That also sets the priority: this is not a live outage anyone is hitting, it is a feature that has never worked.

It is worth correcting the record explicitly, because I got it wrong twice: I first described this function as failing at the *last* step, after the ZIP was built and uploaded, with the lodgement silently unrecorded. Both halves were wrong. It fails at the *first* data step, and there is no lodgement obligation here to miss.

## What resolving it actually requires — a design decision, not a patch

Two distinct questions, and neither should be answered by adding columns to make the query compile:

1. **Where does apprentice demographic data live?** DOB, sex, address and postcode look like `people` fields, not `apprentices` fields — an apprentice is a role a person holds. Sourcing them from `people` is probably right, but that is a schema judgement, not a rename.
2. **Where should unit-level AVETMISS data live?** `subject_enrolments` has never existed. AVETMISS NAT files need per-unit enrolment and outcome records, and the estate already has `/vet/units` as the register and `/competencies` as per-apprentice progress. Whether the export reads those or needs its own table is the real question.

Also: `zip_url` will be null even once the query works, because the `avetmiss-exports` bucket does not exist.

## Rehearsal shim — deliberately not a migration

To isolate and prove the one-line `claims` fix, the rehearsal harness applies `scripts/e2e-rehearsal/avetmiss-export.rehearsal-only-shim.sql` — nullable columns plus a throwaway table, applied **only** to the disposable database.

**It is not a migration and must not become one.** It exists so the crash fix could be positive-controlled (reverted → `HTTP 500 claims is not defined`; fixed → `HTTP 200` with `avetmiss_exports.lodged_by` matching the caller in the DB). Promoting it would encode a schema nobody designed.

issues.body:
Operator observed: There is still no clear way for a client to connect SMTP, Google or Azure email and send from their own account. The operator notes this has been raised more than twenty times.

**Route/surface:** client email-account settings (crm7)

Directive: D-80 (2026-08-13)

## Why filed in crm7 (cross-app reasoning, as required)
Connecting a client's own email account (SMTP / Google / Azure) is a client-facing settings capability, most naturally surfaced in crm7's settings area where the client already manages their profile/org settings and where outbound communications (see item 29, `/communications/compose`) are sent from.

## Acceptance criteria
- A client can connect their own SMTP credentials, or OAuth-connect a Google or Azure email account, from crm7 settings.
- Once connected, outbound communications sent through crm7 (e.g. via `/communications/compose`) can be sent FROM the client's own connected account, not only from a shared platform sender.
- The connection flow is durable (reconnect/refresh handled) rather than a one-time token that silently breaks.

## Mandatory before merge
- **Validation loop:** both — §9.1 (an email actually sends via the connected account, verified end-to-end) and §9.2 (the connection UI is clear and discoverable, given this has been raised 20+ times without resolution).
- **Equivalence target:** An email sent via a connected client account arrives with that account as the sender (verified against the client's actual mailbox/sent folder), not just recorded as "connected" in the database.
- **Cross red-team:** bsuite-auth-guardian
- **Skills to load:** auth-supabase, auth-oauth-native-app-flows

issues.body:
Operator observed: Change-of-year records, wage-anniversary reminders and notices to apprentice and host are missing.

**Route/surface:** change-of-year / wage-anniversary tracking (crm7)

Directive: D-80 (2026-08-13)

## Related prior work (not a duplicate)
crm7#1279 ("Change of Year rollover page has no way to create the first batch — persist logic is real but bootstrap is missing", closed COMPLETED 2026-07-30) fixed a narrower gap: the existing `/admin/change-of-year` page had real persist logic but no way to create the first batch. This item is broader — it covers the wage-anniversary REMINDER and NOTICE capability (to both apprentice and host), which #1279 does not address.

## Cross-reference: crm7 half of D-68
Directive D-68 (filed in parallel in GaryOcean428/R80.4) rules that competency-based progression, anniversary reminders, and change-of-year notices belong in crm7, not in the R80.4 rate calculator — R80.4's calculation is point-in-time (what an apprentice is worth NOW), and the ongoing records/reminders/notices tracking this item covers are the crm7-side counterpart of that ruling. Search R80.4 issues for "competency-based progression" / "D-68" to find the calculator-side ruling issue.

## Acceptance criteria
- Wage-anniversary dates are tracked per apprentice (derived from their training contract), independent of any competency-based progression logic.
- A reminder mechanism fires ahead of each wage-anniversary / change-of-year date.
- A notice capability exists that can notify both the apprentice and the host employer of an upcoming or completed change-of-year event.

## Mandatory before merge
- **Validation loop:** §9.1 output-equivalence — reminders/notices must fire based on real anniversary dates derived from the training contract, not a manually re-entered date.
- **Equivalence target:** A reminder/notice generated by this feature reflects the same anniversary date as the underlying training contract record — no drift between the two.
- **Cross red-team:** bsuite-user-advocate
- **Skills to load:** biz-au-apprenticeship, general-dry-one-shot-architecture

Operator observed: How does the system "create a claim" when the claim actually lives on CTF's (Construction Training Fund's) portal? Only federal claims have a direct system connection, via ADMS (Australian Apprenticeship Data Management System). A "create claim" action that implies the claim is submitted end-to-end through crm7 is misleading for any state/CTF-administered funding source.

**Route/surface:** funding / claims creation flow (wherever "create a claim" is offered)

## Acceptance criteria
- The "create a claim" action is scoped correctly per funding source: for federal ADMS-connected claims, it can genuinely submit/track via the ADMS connection; for CTF or other portal-administered funding, the UI is explicit that this only prepares/records the claim locally and does not submit it — the operator still has to lodge it on CTF's own portal.
- No UI copy implies a direct system-to-system submission exists where it does not.
- The distinction between "federal (ADMS-connected)" and "state/CTF (portal-only)" claim types is visible to the user making the claim.

## Mandatory before merge
- **Validation loop:** §9.2 visual-equivalence — the UI copy/flow must correctly represent which claim types are truly connected vs. portal-only.
- **Equivalence target:** UI framing matches the real integration boundary: ADMS = federal apprenticeship data connection; CTF and equivalent state funds = no direct submission, portal-only.
- **Cross red-team:** bsuite-user-advocate

Operator observed: `/pipeline/kanban` should pull from conduit rather than holding its own data.

**Route/surface:** `/pipeline/kanban`

Directive: D-80 (2026-08-13)

> D-62: "Fix the class, not the page."

## Possible regression, not a fresh finding
crm7#1268 ("[architecture] /pipeline/kanban uses crm7's own pipeline_cards table with no link to conduit — one-shot violation (register #22)") reported this EXACT defect and was closed as **COMPLETED on 2026-07-28**. The operator is re-reporting the identical problem on 2026-08-13 as still present. Either the fix never actually shipped to the surface the operator is using, or it has regressed. This issue exists to make the CURRENT, observed state visible and trackable (D-60) — it does not assume #1268's fix was wrong, only that the defect is observably still there. Whoever picks this up should first verify whether #1268's merged change reached production before re-deriving a fix (see "merged is not applied" as a known failure class in this codebase).

## Acceptance criteria
- `/pipeline/kanban` reads and writes through `conduit_*` tables (or conduit's API), with no independent `pipeline_cards` store as the source of truth.
- Verify in the LIVE/production database (not just the migration files) that crm7's pipeline board and conduit's data are the same rows, not parallel copies.
- Confirm whether #1268's fix shipped to production; if it did and this has regressed, note the regression point (e.g. a later PR that reintroduced the local table).

## Mandatory before merge
- **Validation loop:** §9.1 output-equivalence — a card change made in conduit must be visible on `/pipeline/kanban` and vice versa, with no independent state.
- **Equivalence target:** `/pipeline/kanban` and conduit's own pipeline view render from the identical underlying rows — verified live, not just via code review.
- **Cross red-team:** bsuite-platform
- **Skills to load:** general-dry-one-shot-architecture, supabase:supabase

Operator observed: Training-plan units appear associated to the apprentice — cross-cutting, and the DRY one-shot policy also applies.

**Route/surface:** training-plan / units-of-competency association (surfaces: training-plan record, apprentice profile)

Directive: D-80 (2026-08-13)

> D-62: "Fix the class, not the page."

This affects at least 2 surfaces: the training-plan record and the apprentice profile page (units render/associate on both). The fix must correct the underlying entity association (units belong to the training contract / qualification, not the person), not just hide the symptom on one page.

## Related-but-distinct existing issues (not duplicates)
crm7#1569 (UX duplication of units, doesn't pull from TGA), crm7#662 (feature: assign units to training periods + competency-based progression), crm7#1385 (training catalogue RTO scope) all touch "units of competency" but none addresses this specific defect: units are wired to the apprentice (a person) as the owning entity, when the correct DRY owner is the training contract / qualification record. This is a data-model/entity-ownership defect, not a UX-duplication, feature-scope, or catalogue-scope issue.

## Acceptance criteria
- Units of competency are associated to the training contract / qualification entity, not directly to the apprentice person record.
- Anywhere units currently render "off" the apprentice record is updated to read through the training-contract/qualification association instead.
- No mirror/duplicate unit-association table is introduced — one owning relationship, read everywhere else.

## Mandatory before merge
- **Validation loop:** §9.1 output-equivalence — unit data displayed via the apprentice profile and via the training-plan record must resolve from the same underlying association, not two separate reads.
- **Equivalence target:** Matches the DRY one-shot architecture doctrine (`docs/20260227-dry-one-shot-architecture-v1.02A.md`) — one owning entity for units-of-competency association, read (not duplicated) everywhere else.
- **Cross red-team:** bsuite-platform

**Source:** operator full-spectrum review, 2026-08-11 (Tier 5, minus the audit trail and localStorage items filed separately as crm7#1643 and crm7#1644).

Grouped — these are ops/DX hygiene and are cheapest done together.

## 5.2 — Edge functions log via raw `console.*` (142 instances), unstructured
Fine for reading Supabase logs by eye; useless for correlation. A shared `_shared/log.ts` emitting structured JSON with a **request id** would make the pg_cron / tga incident class (#1617, #1377) diagnosable — those are precisely the failures where you need to follow one invocation across several log lines.

## 5.4 — 578 migrations, 63 quarantined
Beyond the open #1506 / #1525, consider a **squash-to-baseline cadence**. The `20260807_prod_baseline_schema_dump.sql` mechanism already exists and works; the question is how often to fold. Replay time and the tolerant-replay hazard both grow with the tail.

## 5.5 — RLS pattern drift across 2,271 policies
Inconsistent anon-revoke styles mean grep-based audits produce false positives, which trains people to ignore them. The linters exist; a one-time normalisation sweep would make the greps trustworthy. Related standing hazard: **three protections on `catalog.qualifications` existed only in production and in no committed file** — normalise against the baseline dump, not against `pg_policy`.

## 5.6 — `.env` drift: 18 vars referenced vs 21 documented
A small CI script comparing `import.meta.env.*` usage against `.env.example` keeps this permanently aligned. Cheap, and it stops the documented set drifting into fiction — which is the same failure as the `dependency-audit` script entry that pointed at a deleted file (fixed in crm7#1627).

## 5.7 — PDF triple-stack needs a documented boundary
`@react-pdf/renderer` (render), `pdf-lib` (sign/fill), `react-pdf` (view). These are genuinely different jobs and the stack is defensible — **but it is not written down anywhere**, so a fourth will appear. Document which is for what in CONTRIBUTING.

Note this now interacts with the colour rule: the react-pdf exemption triggers on a real **import** as of crm7#1623, so a file using `pdf-lib` does *not* get it. That is correct — pdf-lib takes normalised `rgb(0-1)` values and pure black there is still banned — but it is a sharp edge worth documenting alongside the boundary.

## Mandatory before merge (FF-SELF-VALIDATION-20260507)
- **Validation loop**: §9.1 output-equivalence
- **Equivalence target**: per item — structured log lines carry a correlatable request id across an invocation; the `.env` check fails on a deliberately undocumented var; the RLS sweep leaves grep audits with zero false positives on a sample
- **Cross red-team**: claude-code verifies the `.env` gate FAILS before trusting it
- **Skills to load**: db-supabase, supabase-postgres-best-practices, check-security
- **Self-report on divergence**: yes

**Acceptance criteria:** each sub-item shipped with its gate demonstrated failing, or explicitly deferred with a reason recorded here.

A grouped issue rather than six thin ones — these are related surface-quality items and are best picked up together when someone is in this area. ## 4.2 — Empty states: 322 instances, no shared component Quality will be inconsistent by construction. One `EmptyState` with icon / message / CTA slots standardises it. Worth doing before the count grows; also the natural home for the "you have no X yet, here is how to make one" copy that currently varies per page. ## 4.3 — Mobile tables have no column-hiding or horizontal-scroll strategy Complements the open #1270 / #1271. **Field officers are the most mobile-bound persona in this product** — they are on-site, on a phone, and the tables they need are the widest. Pairs naturally with the virtualisation work in #1628 since both touch `EnhancedDataTable`'s render path. ## 4.4 — `loading="lazy"` on images Trivial, unstarted. Note that the a11y sweep found **zero raw `` without alt** in `src`, so images are largely rendered through components — apply the attribute at the component, not by hand at 300 call sites. ## 4.5 — Command palette / global search across 443 pages Check whether one exists first. The valuable question is not "is there a cmd-K" but **"does it cover entities, or only routes"** — with 443 pages, navigating by route name is already hard; what a user actually wants is to type an apprentice's name. ## 4.6 — Keyboard shortcuts and focus outlines for the bulk flows Timesheet approval queues and claim review are processed in volume by power users. These are the flows where keyboard support stops being an accessibility nicety and becomes a throughput feature. The new jsx-a11y gate (#1633) covers *static* violations; it cannot tell you that a queue is unusable without a mouse. ## 4.7 — Verify the date-format preference is applied everywhere `au`/`us` preference exists — good. **Spot-check reports and PDFs specifically**: they typically bypass React hooks and format dates directly, so a preference implemented in a hook will silently not apply there. An Australian user seeing `03/04/2026` rendered as US month-first on an exported report is a real misreading, not a cosmetic one — and on a compliance document it is worse. ## Suggested order 4.7 first (it is a correctness bug, cheap to check), then 4.2 (compounding), then 4.3 with #1628, then 4.6, 4.5, 4.4. ## Mandatory before merge (FF-SELF-VALIDATION-20260507) - **Validation loop**: §9.2 visual-equivalence - **Equivalence target**: per item — a screenshot pair at 375 and 1440 for the table and empty-state work; for 4.7, an exported PDF and a report screenshot showing the preferred format - **Cross red-team**: copilot checks 4.7 on an EXPORT path, not only in-app - **Skills to load**: web-ui-ux-patterns, machine-design-web-guidelines, data-pdf - **Self-report on divergence**: yes **Acceptance criteria:** each sub-item either shipped with evidence or explicitly deferred with a reason recorded here.

issues.body:
**Source:** operator full-spectrum review, 2026-08-11 (Tier 5.1).

## Finding

**352 `localStorage` references across 79 files**, including auth tokens and offline caches.

## The part that makes this more than tidiness

`AUTH_CANONICAL.md` and `CLAUDE.md` carry a hard forbidden-pattern list for auth storage: no `cookie-backed storage`, no `the former cross-app cookie domain`, no `storageKey: 'legacy shared auth storage key'`. Today that rule is enforced by **review and memory**. With 352 scattered call sites, nothing mechanically prevents the next one.

**Centralising behind one typed module makes the auth rules lintable** — a single chokepoint can be asserted in a contract test, and a bare `localStorage.setItem` outside it becomes a lint error. That converts a doctrine into a gate, which is the same move that worked for colours and a11y.

## Also solved by the same change

- **Namespacing** — no collisions between features.
- **Quota handling** — `localStorage` throws on quota exceeded and in Safari private mode. With 352 unguarded sites, at least some will be unhandled; that is an unhandled exception in a render path.
- **Schema versioning for offline caches** — a cache written by an old build and read by a new one is a shape mismatch with no migration story. This codebase has just been bitten twice by a *type* that disagreed with its data (crm7#1595); a persisted cache is the same hazard with a longer memory.
- **SSR/test safety** — one place to guard `typeof window === 'undefined'`.

## Approach

1. Inventory the 352 by purpose: auth, user preference, offline cache, UI state, one-off.
2. Write the typed module with namespacing, quota handling, JSON safety, and a version tag per cache key.
3. Migrate by category, auth first — it is the smallest group and the highest stakes.
4. **Then add the lint rule**, and only then. A rule added before the migration is red on day one and gets switched off by day two.
5. Keys already in use must be read at their existing names or users lose state on deploy. Plan the read-old/write-new window explicitly.

## Note
`crm7-has-completed-onboarding` is one of these keys and is load-bearing for e2e (seeded via `addInitScript` to suppress the onboarding wizard). Renaming keys will break test harnesses that seed them — grep the e2e suite before changing any name.

## Mandatory before merge (FF-SELF-VALIDATION-20260507)
- **Validation loop**: §9.1 output-equivalence
- **Equivalence target**: existing users keep their stored state across the deploy (read-old/write-new proven with a fixture), and a bare `localStorage` call outside the module fails lint
- **Cross red-team**: copilot verifies the auth forbidden-pattern list is now mechanically enforced, not just documented
- **Skills to load**: auth-supabase, code-quality-enforcement, web-zustand
- **Self-report on divergence**: yes

**Acceptance criteria:** one typed storage module, auth keys migrated first, quota and SSR guarded, no state lost on deploy, and the forbidden-pattern rules enforced by lint rather than by memory.
issues.title: [P3] 352 localStorage call sites across 79 files — centralising makes the auth forbidden-pattern rules lintable

issues.body:
**Source:** operator full-spectrum review, 2026-08-11 (Tier 5.3). Ranked above the rest of Tier 5 because it is compliance-adjacent.

## Finding

`auditService` exists; its coverage is *"not universal"*. For a GTO platform, an audit trail that covers most mutations is not an audit trail — the value is in being able to say *"every change to this record is recorded"*, and one uncovered path makes that sentence false.

## Enumerate, then assert

Name the compliance-critical mutations and assert each writes an audit row. The review's starting list, worth extending:

- **Claim approve** — money leaves on this
- **Payroll export** — the figures that become payments
- **Rate change** — feeds the charge rate and the BOOT position
- **Document sensitivity flip** (crm7#1531) — changes who can see identity documents
- **Tenant switch** — who was acting as whom, the first question in any incident

Add from this session's work: **document generation** (crm7#1595 — a generated document is a record issued to a person), and **compliance record creation** (LLN assessments, WHS audits — crm7#1597 just gated these, and a compliance record with no provenance is weak evidence).

## The verification that actually holds

**One pgTAP test per action**, asserting the audit row exists after the mutation — not a unit test of `auditService` itself. The service being correct proves nothing about whether a given code path calls it. The gap is always the call site.

Two cautions from this codebase:
1. The pgTAP harness runs with `session_replication_role='replica'`, which **suppresses triggers**. If any audit row is written by a trigger, the assertion will pass vacuously or fail confusingly. See `60_org_member_provisioning.sql` and suite 75 for the narrow `SET LOCAL session_replication_role = 'origin'` pattern.
2. Assert the **row**, not the service call. A spy on `auditService.log()` proves the code called a function; it does not prove a row landed, survived RLS, and carried the right tenant.

## Worth deciding at the same time

Retention. crm7#1599 shipped audit/error-log retention with archive-then-delete, and the operator ruling is 7 years for training records. If an audit row is the evidence that a compliance action happened, its retention must not be shorter than the record it describes.

## Mandatory before merge (FF-SELF-VALIDATION-20260507)
- **Validation loop**: §9.1 output-equivalence
- **Equivalence target**: for each enumerated action, a pgTAP test that performs the mutation and asserts the audit row — demonstrated FAILING first with the audit call removed
- **Cross red-team**: claude-code confirms each test asserts a row rather than a spy
- **Skills to load**: bsuite-rls-authz-red-team, supabase-postgres-best-practices, general-iso27001-docs
- **Self-report on divergence**: yes

**Acceptance criteria:** every enumerated compliance-critical mutation has a passing pgTAP audit-row assertion that has been observed failing, and audit retention is at least as long as the records it evidences.
issues.title: [P2][compliance] Audit-trail coverage is 'not universal' — enumerate the compliance-critical mutations and assert a row per action

issues.body:
**Source:** operator full-spectrum review, 2026-08-11 (Tier 2.5).

## Finding

| Marker | Count |
|---|---|
| `any` | 624 |
| `@ts-expect-error` | **256** |
| non-null assertion (`!`) | 126 |

Much of the `any` is the generated `src/types/supabase.ts` (21,646 lines) and is not worth chasing.

**The 256 `@ts-expect-error` are the interesting number.** Each one is a *real type error that was suppressed*. Unlike `any`, which is often laziness, `@ts-expect-error` marks a place where the compiler objected and someone overrode it — so each is either a genuine library-typing gap, or a bug wearing a comment.

## Why this is worth a pass, not just a note

This session found two crashes caused by a **hand-written type that disagreed with the database** (`DocumentTemplate`/`DocumentRecord`, crm7#1595). The compiler could not help, because the wrong shape was asserted with confidence. `@ts-expect-error` is the same failure mode made explicit: the type system knows something is wrong and has been told to be quiet.

## Approach

1. **Triage, do not bulk-fix.** Classify each: (a) upstream typing gap — keep, with a comment naming the library and version, (b) genuinely unsafe — fix, (c) stale — the error no longer occurs, so the directive itself is now an error under `noUnusedTsExpectError`. **Start by finding (c)** — those are free, and TypeScript will report them for you.
2. **Ratchet the rest.** This repo already ratchets ESLint (`eslint-baseline.json`) and pure-colour counts (`theme-c1-baseline.txt`). The same mechanism applies: record today's count, fail on an increase. That stops the number growing while the backlog is worked.
3. A bare `@ts-expect-error` with no description should be a lint error going forward — `@typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment` supports `descriptionFormat`. A suppression with no reason is unreviewable.

## Related, same family
- 126 non-null assertions: each asserts the compiler is wrong about nullability. In a codebase where a hand-written type was wrong about a whole table, that assumption deserves checking.
- Over-memoization (Tier 2.6): 1,303 `useMemo`/`useCallback` with React Compiler enabled, most now redundant. Low priority — stop adding new ones, note it in CONTRIBUTING.

## Mandatory before merge (FF-SELF-VALIDATION-20260507)
- **Validation loop**: §9.1 output-equivalence
- **Equivalence target**: `pnpm typecheck` stays exit 0; the count of `@ts-expect-error` is recorded in a baseline and CI fails on an increase; category (c) reaches zero
- **Cross red-team**: copilot spot-checks 10 kept suppressions for a stated reason
- **Skills to load**: code-quality-enforcement, check-code-quality
- **Self-report on divergence**: yes

**Acceptance criteria:** stale suppressions removed, remaining ones carry a reason, and a ratchet prevents the count rising.
issues.title: [P3] 256 @ts-expect-error suppressions — triage the stale ones and ratchet the rest

**Source:** operator full-spectrum review, 2026-08-11 (Tier 2.1). Re-verified: `src/App.tsx` is **4,019 lines** — grown from the review's 3,859 during today's route work.

## Finding

One file holds routes, auth wiring, wizard management and feature gates. 362 lazy routes are declared inline.

## Why this is worth doing, beyond tidiness

**It mechanically unlocks per-route error boundaries (#1629).** Today there are 3 boundaries for 443 pages, so one render error in a lazy route blanks a whole section. Threading a boundary through 362 inline route declarations means touching this file 362 times. Extracting per-domain route manifests first turns that into a change to one wrapper.

Sequence: **2.1 then 1.5.** Doing them the other way round is the expensive order.

## Shape

Extract route manifests per domain — people, financial, compliance, WHS, documents, portal, settings — into config modules, leaving `App.tsx` to compose them. The route objects are already uniform (`path`, `component`, `routeName`, `permission`), which is what makes this tractable.

## Two guards that must not regress

1. **`src/__tests__/inpage-link-route-coverage.test.ts`** (#1578) and **`nav-route-coverage.test.ts`** (#1098) both parse `App.tsx` **as text**, matching `path="..."`. Moving route declarations into other files will make both guards silently see fewer routes — and a coverage guard that reads an empty set passes. **Update both to walk the manifests, and confirm they still fail when a route is removed** before trusting them again. This is the single biggest risk in the change.
2. Route ORDER is load-bearing in wouter. `/leads/scoring` must precede `/leads/:id`, `/compliance/whs-audits/create` must precede `/compliance/whs-audits`. Composition must preserve order within a domain and the relative order of domains.

## Do not

Combine this with behaviour changes. It is a pure move; anything else in the same PR makes a 4,000-line diff unreviewable.

## Mandatory before merge (FF-SELF-VALIDATION-20260507)
- **Validation loop**: §9.1 output-equivalence
- **Equivalence target**: the set of registered `(path, permission)` pairs is IDENTICAL before and after — dump both and diff, do not eyeball
- **Cross red-team**: claude-code verifies both route-coverage guards still FAIL when a route is deleted post-refactor
- **Skills to load**: bsuite-page-grid-layout, code-quality-enforcement, test-qa-and-verification
- **Self-report on divergence**: yes

**Acceptance criteria:** identical route set, both guards still demonstrated failing on a removed route, order preserved, and no behaviour change in the same PR.
issues.title: [P3] App.tsx is 4,019 lines — extract per-domain route manifests (unlocks per-route error boundaries)

issues.body:
**Blocks the most valuable rule in the new accessibility gate (PR #1633).**

## The problem

`jsx-a11y/label-has-associated-control` **crashes the entire ESLint run**:

```
TypeError: (0 , _minimatch.default) is not a function
Occurred while linting src/components/admin/GrantsConsole.tsx:299
Rule: "jsx-a11y/label-has-associated-control"
    at traverseChildren (.../lib/util/mayContainChildComponent.js:38)
```

An ESM/CJS interop break against the `minimatch` version resolved here.

## Why it cannot be version-fixed today

- `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y@6.10.2` is **the latest published version — there is no 7.x.**
- It declares `peerDependencies: { "eslint": "^3 || ^4 || ^5 || ^6 || ^7 || ^8 || ^9" }`.
- **crm7 runs ESLint 10.8.0.**

So the plugin does not claim to support ESLint 10 at all. This rule is simply the first place that shows.

## Why it is the expensive one to lose

It is the rule that would cover **form-label association** — the review's Tier 3.3 finding of 32 `<label>` elements against hundreds of forms. Screen-reader users cannot complete an unlabelled onboarding wizard.

Every other recommended rule is now enforced (23 at `error`, 10 at `warn`). **This is the only gap in the gate, and it is the largest surface.**

## Options, roughly in order of preference

1. **`pnpm patch` the interop.** The repo already ships a `patches/` directory, so the mechanism exists. Smallest change: fix the `minimatch` default-import in `mayContainChildComponent.js`. Verify by enabling the rule and confirming it both runs *and* reports on a known-unlabelled form.
2. **Pin `minimatch`** to a version whose export shape the plugin expects, via a pnpm override. Check the blast radius first — `minimatch` is a common transitive dependency.
3. **Upstream it.** Open an issue/PR on `jsx-a11y` for ESLint 10 support. Correct, but not a plan on its own.
4. **A targeted local rule.** This repo already maintains five bespoke ESLint rules in `eslint-rules/`, so a narrow "label must reference a control" rule is within its normal practice. Least leverage, most control.

## Verify properly whichever route is taken

**Positive-control it.** Write a fixture with a genuinely unlabelled input, confirm the rule *fires*, then fix the fixture and confirm it goes quiet. A rule that runs without crashing is not the same as a rule that works — and the crash currently masks whether it would report anything useful on this codebase at all.

## Mandatory before merge (FF-SELF-VALIDATION-20260507)
- **Validation loop**: §9.1 output-equivalence
- **Equivalence target**: `label-has-associated-control` runs to completion across `src/**` AND is demonstrated firing on an unlabelled-input fixture
- **Cross red-team**: claude-code re-runs the full lint to confirm no other rule from the plugin has the same latent crash
- **Skills to load**: code-quality-enforcement, research-best-practice
- **Self-report on divergence**: yes

**Acceptance criteria:** the rule is enabled and enforced, its real violation count on `src/**` is recorded, and the chosen fix is documented so a dependency bump does not silently undo it.
issues.title: [P2][a11y] jsx-a11y label-has-associated-control crashes on ESLint 10 — the form-label rule is the one gap in the new gate

**Source:** operator full-spectrum review, 2026-08-11. Re-verified: **3** `<ErrorBoundary>` usages in `src/App.tsx`.

## Finding

Three boundaries for **443 pages**. One render error in a lazy route can blank an entire section rather than the page that failed.

## Why it is cheap here

`src/App.tsx` already wraps every lazy route in `retryImport` and a `<S>` Suspense helper. A per-route boundary drops into that same wrapper — the seam exists, and Sentry is already wired to receive.

## The dependency worth respecting

`src/App.tsx` is **4,019 lines** (re-verified — it has grown; the review measured 3,859). Threading a boundary through 362 route declarations by hand means touching that file 362 times.

**Extracting per-domain route manifests first makes this mechanical** rather than a 362-line diff. The two should be sequenced: extraction, then boundaries. See the App.tsx decomposition issue.

## Related, same class

~23 silent `.catch(() => {})` handlers (the review's count; my narrower grep found 2 — **trust the review, my pattern was blunt**). Each is a debugging dead end: an error that reaches one of these leaves no trace anywhere, which is how a defect survives a log review. Worth a sweep in the same pass — every one either handles the error, reports it, or explains in a comment why discarding is correct.

## What a good boundary does here

Not just "something went wrong". It should name the route, offer a recovery action (retry / back to dashboard, as the inline 404 already does), and report to Sentry with the route in the tags — otherwise a section-level failure is indistinguishable from a blank page in the logs.

## Mandatory before merge (FF-SELF-VALIDATION-20260507)
- **Validation loop**: §9.2 visual-equivalence
- **Equivalence target**: a deliberately-thrown error in one lazy route renders a scoped fallback with the rest of the shell intact — screenshot — and appears in Sentry tagged with that route
- **Cross red-team**: claude-code verifies the boundary is per-route, not a single higher one that merely looks scoped
- **Skills to load**: machine-vercel-react-best-practices, test-playwright
- **Self-report on divergence**: yes

**Acceptance criteria:** a render error is contained to its own route with a recovery action and a tagged Sentry report; the silent-catch sweep is complete with each survivor justified in a comment.
issues.title: [P2] 3 error boundaries for 443 pages — one lazy-route error blanks a whole section

issues.body:
**Source:** operator full-spectrum review, 2026-08-11. Re-verified: `src/lib/avetmiss/` has **17 source files and 2 test files**.

## The gap, ranked by consequence

| Area | Coverage | If it breaks silently |
|---|---|---|
| **AVETMISS** | ~12% (2/17) | A wrong NAT file is lodged with NCVER. Annual statutory obligation for a GTO. |
| **Xero adapter** | **0%** (1,153 LOC) | Invoices, payments and credit notes desync from the accounting ledger. |
| Compliance lib | ~20% | Compliance state reported wrongly to a regulator or a host. |
| Payroll | ~40% | Wage error. |
| Awards | ~40% | Wrong penalty/allowance — an underpayment. |

The repo's own standard (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`) is **70% for critical paths**. These are not adjacent to the critical path; they *are* it. AVETMISS and Xero are the two places where a silent defect stops being a bug and becomes an incident with a regulator or an accountant.

## Why "0% on the Xero adapter" is worse than it sounds

Untested integration code fails **quietly and late**: a field mapping drifts, a sync reports success, and the discrepancy surfaces at reconciliation weeks later, by which time the wrong number is in someone's books. There is already a known Xero UI-wiring gap (#1320) — the adapter beneath it has never been exercised by a test.

## Approach — do not chase the percentage

A coverage number is satisfiable without testing anything that matters. Target the **decisions**, not the lines:

1. **AVETMISS**: the NAT file *contents*. Fixture in → expected NAT rows out, per file type, including the demographic edge cases AVETMISS is fussy about. Validation-failure paths matter as much as the happy path — a silently-dropped record is the failure mode.
2. **Xero**: the adapter's mapping in both directions, plus the error/retry paths. Mock at the HTTP boundary, not at the adapter's own interface, or the test asserts the mock.
3. **Awards/payroll**: reconcile against the **published pay guide**, not a test-local re-derivation of the same logic — see `biz-au-award-modelling`. A test that re-implements the engine's arithmetic proves only that the arithmetic is self-consistent.

## Then hold the line

Wire a coverage threshold in CI (**see the CI wire-up issue** — `test:coverage` exists and no threshold is enforced), scoped to these paths first rather than globally, so the number cannot slide back.

## Mandatory before merge (FF-SELF-VALIDATION-20260507)
- **Validation loop**: §9.1 output-equivalence
- **Equivalence target**: AVETMISS NAT output matches a known-good fixture byte-for-byte per file type; Xero mappings round-trip; award figures reconcile to the published pay guide
- **Cross red-team**: claude-code confirms the tests exercise the SHIPPED path, not a re-derivation
- **Skills to load**: biz-au-award-modelling, biz-xero-integration, test-qa-and-verification
- **Self-report on divergence**: yes

**Acceptance criteria:** AVETMISS and Xero reach the 70% standard on decision coverage, a CI threshold prevents regression, and each suite is demonstrated failing against a deliberately broken mapping before being trusted.
issues.title: [P1] AVETMISS ~12% and Xero adapter 0% tested — the two paths where a silent defect becomes a regulatory or accounting incident

issues.body:
**Source:** operator full-spectrum review, 2026-08-11. Counts re-verified 2026-08-11: **11 API routes** confirmed.

## Finding

| Surface | State |
|---|---|
| `api/` routes | **3 of 11** verify JWTs; **2** rate-limit |
| `/api/rpc/[...path].ts` | allowlists one RPC but does **not validate the token itself** |
| `/api/error-report.ts` | **no auth at all** |
| `tga-*` edge functions | no auth guard |
| Edge functions | **1 of 36** uses Zod input validation; the rest use manual guards |

## The one to look at first

**`/api/error-report.ts` is unauthenticated.** Anyone can POST arbitrary error reports. That is a log-flooding and spam vector, and it writes to the same `error_log` another lane is currently mining for recurring-error issue filing (crm7#1600 / bsu#677) — so a flood does not just fill a table, it manufactures GitHub issues.

Worth checking against that lane's finding that `error_log` is already 2,133 rows of which 1,856 are one genuine bug (crm7#1603). Signal-to-noise there is already poor.

## The standard to extend

`AGENTS.md` already mandates rate limiting on AI endpoints, with a documented pattern (`AI_CONFIG.rateLimits`, 429 + `Retry-After`). The rule is right and its scope is too narrow. **Extend it to every mutating endpoint**, and say so in AGENTS.md so the next endpoint inherits it.

Note the existing standard's own warning: *"if you define config, it must be consumed — dead config is a bug."* A rate limiter that is imported but never called is worse than none, because it reads as covered.

## Approach

1. **Enumerate honestly first** — list all 11 routes and all 36 edge functions with their current auth/validation/rate-limit state. Do not trust this table; re-derive it. `tga-*` being pg_cron-invoked (Class D) is a *reason* for a different guard, not for no guard — a cron-only function should still refuse an unauthenticated HTTP caller.
2. **Classify** each: public-by-design / authenticated / service-role / cron-only. Public-by-design should be a very short list and each entry should have a reason.
3. **Fix the unauthenticated mutating ones first**, `error-report` at the front.
4. **Zod at the boundary.** 1 of 36 is the real story here; manual guards drift and are not self-documenting. A shared `_shared/validate.ts` helper makes the 36th as cheap as the 2nd.

## Verification this needs

Per route: an unauthenticated request is **refused** (assert the status, not the absence of a crash), and an over-limit burst returns 429 with `Retry-After`. Prove the limiter fires — a limiter never seen rejecting is not a limiter.

## Mandatory before merge (FF-SELF-VALIDATION-20260507)
- **Validation loop**: §9.1 output-equivalence
- **Equivalence target**: for each mutating endpoint, an unauthenticated call returns 401/403 and an over-limit burst returns 429 — both demonstrated, not asserted
- **Cross red-team**: copilot re-derives the auth matrix independently rather than reading this issue
- **Skills to load**: check-security, bsuite-rls-authz-red-team, auth-supabase
- **Self-report on divergence**: yes

**Acceptance criteria:** every mutating endpoint is either authenticated or documented as public-by-design with a reason; every one is rate-limited; input validation is schema-based at the boundary; and the AGENTS.md standard is widened past AI endpoints.
issues.title: [P1][security] API routes: 3/11 verify JWTs, /api/error-report has no auth, 1/36 edge functions validate input

issues.body:
**Source:** operator full-spectrum review, 2026-08-11. Filed as **Tier 1** despite arriving under "UX polish" — this is a wage-compliance risk, not a nicety.

## Why this is compliance

CRM7 is a multi-state Australian GTO platform. WA is up to **3 hours** behind the eastern states, and DST rules diverge (WA has none; NSW/VIC/SA/TAS do; QLD does not).

Award penalty windows are defined in **local time**: early-morning loadings, night loadings, weekend boundaries, public-holiday boundaries. So:

- A shift recorded 05:30–13:30 **AWST** is 08:30–16:30 **AEDT**. One attracts an early-morning loading; the other does not.
- A Sunday shift starting 23:00 Saturday **AWST** is already Sunday in Sydney.
- A payroll cutoff at "midnight Friday" is three different instants across the estate.

**Getting the timezone wrong changes which penalty rate applies, and therefore what the apprentice is paid.** That is an underpayment or an overcharge, not a rendering bug — and under-payment of an apprentice is exactly the exposure a GTO carries.

## What the review found

The schema **has** timezone columns. There is **no runtime timezone context** — no provider, no per-tenant/per-placement resolution at the point where times are interpreted.

## Establish before fixing (do not assume)

1. **Where are the timezone columns, and are they populated?** Check the baseline dump (`supabase/migrations/baseline/20260807_prod_baseline_schema_dump.sql`), not just the migrations — three protections on another table existed only in production and in no committed file. Then check whether real rows carry a value or a NULL.
2. **How are timesheet times currently stored?** `timestamptz` (an instant, safe) or `time`/`timestamp` (wall-clock, ambiguous)? This determines whether the data is already wrong or merely displayed wrong. They are very different problems: one is a migration, the other is a render fix.
3. **Where does the penalty-window decision actually happen?** `@bsuite/charge-calc` owns rate calculation (R8 owns ALL rate calc — standing ruling). Trace whether it receives a timezone at all, or assumes server/browser local.
4. **What does the interpreter do today?** Find the shift-interpretation path and determine which clock it reads.

## Then decide

- Per-**tenant** timezone, per-**host-employer**, or per-**placement**? A GTO in WA can place an apprentice with a host in SA. The placement's location is what governs the award, not the GTO's head office.
- Display vs calculation: users should see local time; the engine must compute in the *placement's* zone regardless of who is looking.

## Verification this needs

A fixture-based test per state, crossing a DST boundary, asserting the **same instant** produces the correct and *different* penalty outcome per zone. Use real award windows (MA000020 etc. — see `biz-au-award-modelling`), and reconcile against the published pay guide, not a test-local re-derivation.

## Mandatory before merge (FF-SELF-VALIDATION-20260507)
- **Validation loop**: §9.1 output-equivalence
- **Equivalence target**: a shift crossing an early-morning penalty boundary yields the correct loading in AWST, AEST and AEDT, proven against the published pay guide
- **Cross red-team**: claude-code verifies the engine actually receives the zone rather than defaulting
- **Skills to load**: biz-au-award-modelling, biz-au-award-boot, gto-rate-calculation-rules
- **Self-report on divergence**: yes

**Acceptance criteria:** the penalty-window decision is made in the placement's timezone, proven by per-state DST-crossing fixtures; and it is stated explicitly whether any historical data was interpreted in the wrong zone.
issues.title: [P1][compliance] No runtime timezone context — a WA shift read in Sydney time changes which award penalty rate applies

issues.body:
**Found by:** the crm7#1598 lane, 2026-08-11, while building the positive control it was asked for. Not the question it was sent to answer.

**Versions:** `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` 7.1.1, `react` 19.2.8, `eslint` 10.8.0.

## First, the question #1598 asked — answered NO

The React Compiler namespace bug (facebook/react#35280) **does not** reach `react-hooks/refs`, `/purity` or `/immutability` on 7.1.1. Each rule was positive-controlled in bare call form, confirmed enabled for the test path via `--print-config`, then converted character-for-character to `React.useRef` / `React.useMemo` / `React.useState` and re-run. **All three fired identically in both forms.** Exposure: 0.

## But the original attribution in #1582 looks wrong

A *minimal* namespace-form fixture would not reproduce the silence #1582 was built on. So the lane extracted the actual pre-fix `localised-date-input.tsx` (`git show 1de03057^:...`) and ran it verbatim — silent, rule confirmed enabled. Then bisected:

- converting **only** its `React.useEffect` → bare `useEffect`, everything else untouched → **still silent**
- isolating just the `React.forwardRef(function Name(props, ref) {...})` wrapper around a known-working minimal fixture → **reproduced the silence**, for `set-state-in-effect`, `refs` *and* `immutability`, **in both call forms**

So the mechanism behind the one file #1582 used as its evidence was very likely **`React.forwardRef`**, not the receiver-vs-property callee bug it was attributed to. #1582's *fix* stands — the effect was a genuine derived-state violation and refactoring it was right. Its **diagnosis** is the part in doubt.

## Not clean, and deliberately not overclaimed

The lane could not reproduce it for `purity`: a synthetic forwardRef + purity fixture went silent, but the real `sidebar.tsx` — a forwardRef component with a genuine `Math.random()` in `React.useMemo` — fires correctly, before and after that file's edit. So the boundary is uncharacterised.

**Exposure today is nil.** Of the 22 files across `REFS_FILES` / `PURITY_FILES` / `IMMUTABILITY_FILES`, only `sidebar.tsx` uses `forwardRef` at all, and it is the one confirmed still firing. No phantom suppression entries exist because of this.

## Why it still matters

If `forwardRef` can blind these rules, the suppression register undercounts for a **third** independent reason, on top of the two already recorded:
1. synchronous-only detection (setState after `await`/`.then()` is invisible)
2. ~~the namespace bug~~ — ruled out above
3. this

`forwardRef` is pervasive in shadcn primitives. A component authored inside one could carry a real violation that no lint run will ever show.

## What would settle it
- A minimal reproduction that fires without the wrapper and goes silent with it, held constant otherwise, for each affected rule — then upstream it.
- Or: force each rule over every `forwardRef` component in `src/` and compare against the same components mechanically unwrapped.
- Either way, **positive-control first.** A rule that flags nothing in both forms proves nothing, which is the trap that produced the wrong attribution in the first place.

## Mandatory before merge (FF-SELF-VALIDATION-20260507)
- **Validation loop**: §9.1 output-equivalence
- **Equivalence target**: for each rule, a documented fixture pair — wrapped vs unwrapped, identical otherwise — with pasted output showing fires/silent
- **Cross red-team**: claude-code reproduces the fixture pair independently before any claim lands in the register
- **Skills to load**: code-quality-enforcement, research-best-practice
- **Self-report on divergence**: yes

**Acceptance criteria:** the `forwardRef` boundary is characterised or refuted with fixture evidence, and the register header states the real reasons it undercounts rather than implying the namespace bug was the only one.
issues.title: [P3] React.forwardRef may blind react-hooks rules — and crm7#1582's root cause was probably misattributed

**Found by:** crm7#1597 lane, 2026-08-11. Same class as #1597, which fixed only the CREATE affordance.

## Problem

#1597 added `manage_whs_audits` / `manage_lln_assessments` and gated the **create** controls on the compliance registers. The **row-level write** controls were left on the page-level `view_compliance` gate:

- `src/pages/compliance/whs-audits/index.tsx` — the "Advance status" button on each row performs an `UPDATE` on `whs_audits` and is not permission-gated.

RLS `is_gto_staff(tenant_id)` admits `gto_admin` / `gto_staff` / `field_officer` for that UPDATE, so for those roles the write succeeds. For a `view_compliance`-only role that RLS refuses (`training_provider`, `executive`), the button renders and the write fails — the same UI-honesty problem #1597 fixed one control to the left.

## Scope this properly before fixing

Do not patch just this button. Sweep the compliance registers for **every** control that mutates:
- status transitions, inline edits, delete/archive, bulk actions
- the LLN register's equivalents

For each: does the role that can see it hold a permission RLS will honour? Gate on the entity permission (`manage_whs_audits` / `manage_lln_assessments`) introduced by #1597, not on `manage_compliance` — that one excludes `field_officer`, whose job these records are. See #1597 for the full matrix and why.

## The broader question worth answering once

The app permission model and RLS are two independent authorisation systems that have already drifted twice in this cluster. `is_gto_staff()` is a role-set predicate; `usePermissions.ts` is a capability table. Nothing asserts they agree.

A contract test could: for each `manage_*` permission, assert the set of app roles holding it matches the set of `gto_role` values the corresponding RLS predicate admits. That would have caught both #1597 and this issue before either shipped.

## Mandatory before merge (FF-SELF-VALIDATION-20260507)
- **Validation loop**: §9.1 output-equivalence
- **Equivalence target**: for each mutating control, a role WITH the permission completes the write and a role WITHOUT it neither sees the control nor can complete the write — proven at the DB layer by executing as that role, not by reading policy text
- **Cross red-team**: copilot verifies the role-to-RLS mapping independently
- **Skills to load**: bsuite-rls-authz-red-team, supabase-postgres-best-practices, qa-and-verification
- **Self-report on divergence**: yes

**Acceptance criteria:** every mutating control on the compliance registers is gated on a permission whose holders RLS actually admits; ideally a contract test pins app-permissions against RLS role sets so the two cannot drift again.
issues.title: [P2] Compliance registers: row-level write controls still gated on view_compliance (the half #1597 did not cover)

**Found by:** crm7#1597 lane, 2026-08-11. Pre-existing; not caused by #1578 or #1597.

## Problem

`src/pages/portal/host-employer.tsx` offers "WHS Upload" quick actions that navigate to a route the `host_employer` role can never reach:

- L579-580 → `/compliance/whs-audits/create?host_employer_id=...`
- L907-908 → same

`host_employer` holds `view_compliance_dashboard` but **not** `view_compliance`, and never has. The route is gated (`view_compliance` before #1597, `manage_whs_audits` after), so a host employer clicking this gets the Access Denied card.

## Why the route-coverage guard does not catch this

`src/__tests__/inpage-link-route-coverage.test.ts` (added in #1592) asserts every in-page link resolves to a **registered route**. This link does. It is a *permission* dead-end, not a routing dead-end — a third class, after "no route" (#1578) and "nav-config only" (#1098).

That is a gap in the guard worth closing: a link only the wrong audience can see is the same user-facing failure as a 404, and nothing detects it. A static check is feasible — for each in-page link, compare the route's `permission=` against the permissions held by roles that can reach the *linking* page. Non-trivial, but the data is all in `usePermissions.ts` and `App.tsx`.

## Decide

1. **Should host employers be able to request/upload a WHS audit at all?** If yes, they need a permission that reaches the create surface, and RLS must admit their INSERT (`is_gto_staff()` currently does not include them) — that is a product decision plus a migration, not a UI tweak.
2. If no, remove the two quick actions. Do not leave a control that always denies.

## Mandatory before merge (FF-SELF-VALIDATION-20260507)
- **Validation loop**: §9.2 visual-equivalence
- **Equivalence target**: signed in as a `host_employer`-role user on `d.crm.crm7.app`, the WHS Upload action either completes or is absent — screenshot either way
- **Cross red-team**: claude-code verifies the role's permission set against `usePermissions.ts` AND the RLS policy, not just the UI
- **Skills to load**: bsuite-rls-authz-red-team, qa-and-verification
- **Self-report on divergence**: yes

**Acceptance criteria:** no control in the host-employer portal navigates to a surface that role's permissions cannot reach.

## Issue

The Australian apprenticeship system distinguishes between **Standard** and **School-Based** (SAE — school-based apprenticeships and traineeships) apprentices. The crm7 pay-rate hierarchy **does not model School-Based apprentices at all**. The "Standard" label is overloaded to mean both forms, making it impossible to correctly configure rates for SAE cohorts.

## Impact

- Incorrect rate calculations for school-based apprentices
- No way to differentiate SAE rules (e.g., minimum earnings, superannuation treatment) from Standard rules
- Potentially non-compliant with Fair Work obligations

## Evidence

- **Register**: operator-ux-bug-register-v1.00W.md §P1, item #9b (§113)
- **Verification**: 2026-07-28 — identified as missing domain model
- **Status**: Not just a label issue; missing feature in pay-rate hierarchy

## Suggested fix direction

1. Add School-Based as a distinct apprenticeship_type in the data model
2. Update pay-rate configuration to branch rules by type
3. Update UI to display and allow configuration of School-Based rules separately
4. Verify against Fair Work Pay Guide and PACT for any SAE-specific adjustments

## Related

- Related to R80.3 wage calculation, which may need per-type overrides
- Compliance gap: AUS apprenticeship law distinguishes these cohorts; codebase does not

## Mandatory before merge (FF-SELF-VALIDATION-20260507)

- **Validation loop**: §9.1 output-equivalence
- **Equivalence target**: Wage calculation for Standard vs School-Based apprentice at same rate → should differ per Fair Work rules
- **Cross red-team**: copilot verifies domain model against Fair Work Pay Guide §2 School-Based treatment
- **Skills to load**: biz-au-award-modelling, web-forms-validation, architecture
- **Self-report on divergence**: yes (mandatory; do not rationalise gaps)

issues.body:
## Do not flip these to optional — I nearly did, and it would have been a compliance gap

The document-provenance work (crm7#1590) classified bank details, superannuation choice and the TFN declaration as **captured** — structured fields, not documents — and its report recommended a follow-up flipping the two document-kind requirements to `is_required = false` as duplicates.

**Checked the data before implementing it. The recommendation is wrong, and here is why.**

### What is actually there

| Requirement | Kind | Required | Twin? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tax_declaration` | structured_record | yes | ↔ `signed_tfn_declaration_form` |
| `signed_tfn_declaration_form` | **document** | yes | ↔ `tax_declaration` |
| `super_choice` | structured_record | yes | ↔ `super_choice_form` |
| `super_choice_form` | **document** | yes | ↔ `super_choice` |
| `bank_account` | structured_record | yes | **none — no duplication here** |

So two pairs, both required. On the face of it the worker is asked for the same fact twice.

### Why they are not duplicates

**They are different things with different obligations.**

- The **structured record** is the data payroll needs to pay someone: the TFN, the residency status, the threshold claim, the fund and member number. It is what the engine reads.
- The **document** is the *executed instrument*. An employer must retain the signed TFN declaration, and the superannuation standard choice form is likewise a form the employee signs and the employer keeps.

Flipping the documents to optional would remove the prompt for the very artefact that has to be retained. The data would be captured and the signed form would quietly stop being collected — and nobody would notice until someone asked for it.

**`bank_account` genuinely has no document twin**, which is the right shape: an uploaded bank statement is *evidence for* an account number, not the account number, and nothing obliges its retention.

### What should happen instead

**Keep both required. Fix the explanation, not the requirement.**

The onboarding checklist currently presents them as two unrelated line items, which is what makes it read as a duplicate ask. It should say plainly that the fields are what gets used to pay you, and the signed form is what we are obliged to keep — so the worker understands why they are doing both, and staff do not "helpfully" mark one complete.

### What needs an operator ruling

1. **Confirm the retention reading.** I am confident the signed TFN declaration must be retained; I am less certain the superannuation standard choice form carries the same obligation rather than being good practice. That is a question for Braden, not an assumption for me.
2. **Retention periods.** bsuite#1885 §5 already flags that nothing in the platform models retention at all. These two forms are a concrete case: they have a statutory clock and no field to record it.

**No change made.** Recording the reasoning so the next person does not implement the original follow-up on its face.

Refs crm7#1590, bsuite#1885, bsuite#1886

issues.body:
## What happened

While wiring the funding-programs dropdown (crm7#1473) I found that `20260301201400_funding_eligibility.sql` is **recorded in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` but its body never executed** — both tables it creates (`funding_programs`, `funding_milestones`) are absent from production. Fixed for those two tables in #1524.

**I found this by accident.** The repaired pgTAP replay gate rejected my new migration for referencing a table that does not exist. Nothing was looking for this class of defect.

## Why the existing audit does not catch it

`prod-migration-history-audit.yml` flags rows with `statement_count = 0`. This row has a **populated** `statements[]` array — it is the *tracked-but-not-live* class already documented in `supabase/migrations/CLAUDE.md` (2026-07-04 section), which recorded four examples then and explicitly warned:

> "tracked in `schema_migrations` with a non-zero `statement_count`" is **not sufficient evidence a migration was applied**.

So this is a **known class with no automated detector**. Four instances were found by hand in July; a fifth (this one) surfaced in August by accident, five months after it was recorded.

## Scope of the gap

- 585 recorded migrations
- 371 tables in `public`
- No check asserts that a recorded migration's objects actually exist

## What to build

A check that, for every recorded migration, extracts the object names it claims to create (`CREATE TABLE`, `CREATE FUNCTION`, `CREATE INDEX`, `ADD COLUMN`) and asserts each resolves live. Report, do not auto-repair — `CLAUDE.md` is explicit that a zero-statement row must not be auto-repaired, and the same caution applies here.

Known false-positive sources to handle, or the check will be ignored:
- objects deliberately dropped by a **later** migration (walk the whole tree, not one file)
- deliberate tombstones (renamed-not-dropped, e.g. crm7 `ee4f3f39`, `91089e27`)
- conditional DDL inside `DO` blocks / `to_regclass` guards
- migrations targeting the `catalog` schema, whose DDL another submodule owns

## Acceptance criteria

- Running it today reports `20260301201400` as satisfied (after #1524) and lists any others still outstanding
- **Negative control**: with a known-live table's `CREATE` pointed at a nonexistent name, the check fails. A detector that cannot fail is not a detector.
- Output names the migration version, the missing object, and whether a later migration explains the absence

## Validation loop
§9.1 output-equivalence — baseline is the current live catalogue.

## Cross red-team
Verify the negative control genuinely fails before accepting the result.

## Skills to load
`supabase`, `test-verify-before-completion`

Found via crm7#1473 / #1524.

issues.body:
## 17 migrations have been failing in CI, silently, since May

Exposed the moment `pgtap.yml` stopped swallowing failures (PR #1503). They are now **quarantined and visible** in `supabase/migrations/KNOWN-BROKEN-IN-CI.txt`. This issue is the programme to empty that file.

## What was happening

```bash
ERR=$(psql ... | grep ERROR | head -1) || true
if [ -n "$ERR" ]; then echo "::warning::... failed; continuing"; fi
# ...then a second loop recorded EVERY post-baseline version as applied, regardless.
```

Worse than "downgraded to a warning": `$?` came from **grep**, so a psql failure whose message lacked the literal string `ERROR` was never detected at all.

## Why it matters more than 17 broken files

**Every pgTAP run in this repo has executed against a partially-migrated database and reported green.**

Any assertion about an object one of these migrations should have created was **vacuous** — the suite passed *because* the thing under test was absent, which reads identically in the log to it existing and behaving correctly.

That includes the **cross-tenant isolation suites**. Their e2e fixture tenant pair (`20260807100000`) was itself one of the casualties — a migration written *because a real client had been used as the victim in a security test*. So the tests meant to prove isolation fixture-against-fixture have been running with no fixtures. Fixed in #1503; the rest remain.

This is the estate's already-documented **"live but unrebuildable schema"** condition. What is new is that it is now measurable.

## The 17, grouped by cause

**Depends on objects the baseline does not carry (12)**
`20260513120000_ws4_timesheet_state_column_rename` · `20260513130000_add_fk_indexes_phase24.nontx` · `20260514054000_xero_encrypt_tokens_via_vault` (needs Vault) · `20260514120000_drop_orphan_mapd_rate_cache` · `20260515080000_drop_legacy_storage_objects_policies` · `20260707000020_pay_periods_table` · `20260707000021_pay_period_streams_table` (depends on the former) · `20260708000002_fix_award_rates_fk` · `20260708000003_fix_award_rates_classification_fk` · `20260708120000_invoices_bucket_and_xero_contact_id` · `20260729200001_tenant_entity_records` (`column "created_by" does not exist`) · `20260806280000_data_change_sets` (`relation "public.audit_events" does not exist`)

**Seed/fixture data assuming live rows (4)**
`20260704170000_gto_e2e_w6_portal_test_seed` · `20260804221000_unwire_operator_account_from_w6_test_seed` · `20260807076000_report_catalog_p2_seed` · `20260807077000_p4_seed_demo_organisation`

**🚩 A genuine SQL defect — not CI-specific, fails everywhere (1)**
`20260807079000_p6_retire_workers_table` → `ERROR: "array_agg" is an aggregate`. **Fix this one first.** It is not baseline drift; it is broken SQL that happens to have been hidden by the same mechanism.

## The quarantine is a ratchet, not an exemption list

```
a migration NOT listed that FAILS    -> job FAILS   (the protection)
a migration listed that SUCCEEDS     -> job FAILS   (the ratchet)
```

The second rule is what prevents rot: the moment a quarantined migration starts applying, CI demands its line be removed. The list can only shrink, and its length prints every run:

```
::notice::migration replay debt: N quarantined (crm7#1504) — this number must only go down
```

## Order of work

1. **`20260807079000`** — the real SQL defect. Small, and it is not environment-dependent.
2. **The four seed migrations** — make them idempotent/conditional, the way `20260807100000`'s real-client guard was scoped in #1503 (skip when the referenced rows are absent rather than aborting).
3. **The Vault and storage-bucket dependants** — either provision them in CI or guard on their presence.
4. **The baseline-shape mismatches** — these are the real "unrebuildable schema" core and may need a baseline regeneration. Note the standing warning: regenerating a baseline marks all migrations applied, so **nothing replays and every seeded row vanishes**.

## Acceptance

- `KNOWN-BROKEN-IN-CI.txt` contains zero entries.
- A deliberately-broken migration added in a test PR turns the job red **from the migration step** — proven, not assumed.
- The cross-tenant isolation suites are re-run and confirmed to be finding both fixture tenants, with a passing positive control.

**Until that last point is done, treat every historical pgTAP green in this repo as unverified.**
